8	// Capability identifies a feature an adapter provides, such as running an
9	// agent or backing an issue tracker.
10	type Capability string
11	
12	// Capabilities an adapter can advertise in its Manifest.
13	const (
14		CapabilityAgent        Capability = "agent"
15		CapabilityIssueTracker Capability = "issue-tracker"
16	)
17	
18	// Manifest is an adapter's self-description: its id, human-facing name and
19	// description, version, and the capabilities it provides.
20	type Manifest struct {
21		ID           string       `json:"id"`
22		Name         string       `json:"name"`
23		Description  string       `json:"description"`
24		Version      string       `json:"version"`
25		Capabilities []Capability `json:"capabilities"`
26	}
27	
28	// Adapter is the minimal contract every registered adapter satisfies.
29	type Adapter interface {
30		Manifest() Manifest
31	}
32	
33	// Registry holds registered adapters keyed by their manifest id.
34	//
35	// Registry is not safe for concurrent registration: every Register call is
36	// expected at daemon boot, before any goroutine calls Get. Concurrent
37	// Register and Get would race on the underlying map.
38	type Registry struct {
39		adapters map[string]Adapter
40	}
41	
42	// NewRegistry returns an empty Registry ready to Register adapters.
43	func NewRegistry() *Registry {
44		return &Registry{
45			adapters: make(map[string]Adapter),
46		}
47	}
48	
49	// Register adds adapter under its manifest id. It returns an error when the id
50	// is empty or already registered.
51	func (r *Registry) Register(adapter Adapter) error {
52		manifest := adapter.Manifest()
53		if manifest.ID == "" {
54			return fmt.Errorf("adapter id is required")
55		}
56		if _, exists := r.adapters[manifest.ID]; exists {
57			return fmt.Errorf("adapter %q is already registered", manifest.ID)
58		}
59	
60		r.adapters[manifest.ID] = adapter
61		return nil
62	}
63	
64	// Get returns the registered adapter with the given id, or nil and false
65	// when no such adapter exists.
66	func (r *Registry) Get(id string) (Adapter, bool) {
67		p, ok := r.adapters[id]
68		return p, ok
69	}
70	
71	// Manifests returns every registered adapter's manifest, sorted by id.
72	func (r *Registry) Manifests() []Manifest {
73		manifests := make([]Manifest, 0, len(r.adapters))
74		for _, adapter := range r.adapters {
75			manifests = append(manifests, adapter.Manifest())
76		}
77	
78		sort.Slice(manifests, func(i, j int) bool {
79			return manifests[i].ID < manifests[j].ID
80		})
81	
82		return manifests
83	}
84

Constructors returns a fresh instance of every agent adapter the daemon\n// ships, in a stable registration order. Adding a new harness means adding its\n// constructor here (and a domain.AgentHarness constant) — the one edit the\n// daemon, the conformance engine, and the proving ground all pick up.\nfunc Constructors() []adapters.Adapter {\n\treturn []adapters.Adapter{\n\t\tclaudecode.New(),\n\t\tcodex.New(),\n\t\topencode.New(),\n\t\tgrok.New(),\n\t\tdroid.New(),\n\t\tamp.New(),\n\t\tagy.New(),\n\t\tcrush.New(),\n\t\taider.New(),\n\t\tcursor.New(),\n\t\tqwen.New(),\n\t\tcopilot.New(),\n\t\tgoose.New(),\n\t\tauggie.New(),\n\t\tcontinueagent.New(),\n\t\tdevin.New(),\n\t\tcline.New(),\n\t\tkimi.New(),\n\t}\n}\n\n// Build returns a registry populated with the shipped agent adapters, keyed by\n// manifest id. Registration only fails on an empty/duplicate id — a programmer\n// error, not a runtime condition.\nfunc Build() (*adapters.Registry, error) {\n\treg := adapters.NewRegistry()\n\tfor _, a := range Constructors() {\n\t\tif err := reg.Register(a); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"register agent adapter %q: %w\", a.Manifest().ID, err)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn reg, nil\n}\n\n// HarnessAgent pairs a session harness with the adapter that drives it. The\n// harness is the adapter's manifest id, which is also the domain.AgentHarness\n// value a session carries and the `--harness` flag users pass.\ntype HarnessAgent struct {\n\tHarness domain.AgentHarness\n\tAgent   ports.Agent\n}\n\n// Harnessed returns every shipped adapter that drives an agent, paired with its\n// harness, in Constructors() order. An adapter that does not implement\n// ports.Agent is skipped; the conformance Registry check pins that every\n// shipped adapter is in fact agent-capable, so a skip there is a real finding,\n// not silent loss.\nfunc Harnessed() []HarnessAgent {\n\tcons := Constructors()\n\tout := make([]HarnessAgent, 0, len(cons))\n\tfor _, a := range cons {\n\t\tagent, ok := a.(ports.Agent)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tout = append(out, HarnessAgent{\n\t\t\tHarness: domain.AgentHarness(a.Manifest().ID),\n\t\t\tAgent:   agent,\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n"
}

27	// setActivityAPIRequest mirrors the daemon's SetActivityRequest body for
28	// POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/activity. The CLI keeps its own copy so it need
29	// not import httpd.
30	type setActivityAPIRequest struct {
31		State string `json:"state"`
32	}
33	
34	// newHooksCommand builds the hidden `ao hooks <agent> <event>` command that
35	// agent CLIs invoke from their workspace-local hook config. It reads the native
36	// hook payload from stdin and the AO session id from AO_SESSION_ID, derives an
37	// activity state for the event, and reports it to the daemon.
38	//
39	// It is best-effort by design: a hook must never break the user's agent, so a
40	// non-AO session (no AO_SESSION_ID), an event that carries no activity signal,
41	// or an unreachable daemon all exit 0 rather than erroring.
42	func newHooksCommand(ctx *commandContext) *cobra.Command {
43		return &cobra.Command{
44			Use:    "hooks <agent> <event>",
45			Short:  "Receive an agent hook callback (internal)",
46			Hidden: true,
47			Args:   cobra.ExactArgs(2),
48			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
49				return ctx.runHook(cmd.Context(), args[0], args[1])
50			},
51		}
52	}
53	
54	func (c *commandContext) runHook(ctx context.Context, agent, event string) error {
55		sessionID := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("AO_SESSION_ID"))
56		if sessionID == "" {
57			// Not an AO-managed session. Return before reading stdin so a manual
58			// invocation without a piped payload can't block on EOF.
59			return nil
60		}
61		payload, _ := io.ReadAll(c.deps.In) // read error -> empty payload, handled by the deriver.
62	
63		var state string
64		switch agent {
65		case "claude-code", "grok", "continue", "devin":
66			// grok, continue, and devin use the Claude Code compatibility layer for hooks
67			// (see https://docs.x.ai/build/features/skills-plugins-marketplaces
68			// "Grok automatically reads Claude Code ... hooks ...").
69			// Payload shapes match, so we can share the derive logic.
70			s, ok := claudecode.DeriveActivityState(event, payload)
71			if !ok {
72				return nil // event carries no activity signal.
73			}
74			state = string(s)
75		case "codex":
76			s, ok := codexadapter.DeriveActivityState(event, payload)
77			if !ok {
78				return nil // event carries no activity signal.
79			}
80			state = string(s)
81		case "droid":
82			// Droid has no Claude Code compatibility layer and its Notification
83			// payload omits notification_type, so it ships its own deriver.
84			s, ok := droid.DeriveActivityState(event, payload)
85			if !ok {
86				return nil // event carries no activity signal.
87			}
88			state = string(s)
89		case "agy":
90			s, ok := agyadapter.DeriveActivityState(event, payload)
91			if !ok {
92				return nil // event carries no activity signal.
93			}
94			state = string(s)
95		case "cursor":
96			s, ok := cursor.DeriveActivityState(event, payload)
97			if !ok {
98				return nil // event carries no activity signal.
99			}
100			state = string(s)
101		case "qwen":
102			s, ok := qwen.DeriveActivityState(event, payload)
103			if !ok {
104				return nil // event carries no activity signal.
105			}
106			state = string(s)
107		case "copilot":
108			s, ok := copilot.DeriveActivityState(event, payload)
109			if !ok {
110				return nil // event carries no activity signal.
111			}
112			state = string(s)
113		case "goose":
114			s, ok := gooseadapter.DeriveActivityState(event, payload)
115			if !ok {
116				return nil // event carries no activity signal.
117			}
118			state = string(s)
119		case "cline":
120			s, ok := cline.DeriveActivityState(event, payload)
121			if !ok {
122				return nil // event carries no activity signal.
123			}
124			state = string(s)
125		case "kiro":
126			s, ok := kiro.DeriveActivityState(event, payload)
127			if !ok {
128				return nil // event carries no activity signal.
129			}
130			state = string(s)
131		case "kilocode":
132			s, ok := kilocode.DeriveActivityState(event, payload)
133			if !ok {
134				return nil // event carries no activity signal.
135			}
136			state = string(s)
137		case "autohand":
138			s, ok := autohand.DeriveActivityState(event, payload)
139			if !ok {
140				return nil // event carries no activity signal.
141			}
142			state = string(s)
143		default:
144			return nil // unknown agent: nothing to report.
145		}
146	
147		path := "sessions/" + url.PathEscape(sessionID) + "/activity"
148		if err := c.postJSON(ctx, path, setActivityAPIRequest{State: state}, nil); err != nil {
149			// Report to stderr (the agent's hook runner captures it) for diagnosis,
150			// but exit 0: a failed activity report must not disrupt the agent.
151			fmt.Fprintf(c.deps.Err, "ao hooks %s %s: %v\n", agent, event, err)
152		}
153		return nil
154	}

  "content": "// Package activitydispatch is the single source of truth mapping the agent\n// token in `ao hooks <agent> <event>` onto the function that interprets that\n// agent's hook callbacks as an AO activity state.\n//\n// Two callers share it: the hidden `ao hooks` CLI command, which dispatches a\n// live callback, and the adapter conformance engine, which pins that every\n// adapter installing `ao hooks <tok>` callbacks has a deriver registered here —\n// catching the class of bug where an adapter writes callbacks that nothing on\n// the receiving side understands (so its activity is silently never reported).\npackage activitydispatch\n\nimport (\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/agy\"\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/autohand\"\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/claudecode\"\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/cline\"\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex\"\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/copilot\"\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/cursor\"\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/droid\"\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/goose\"\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/kilocode\"\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro\"\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/qwen\"\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/domain\"\n)\n\n// DeriveFunc maps a native agent hook event and its raw stdin payload onto an AO\n// activity state. ok=false means the event carries no activity signal.\ntype DeriveFunc func(event string, payload []byte) (domain.ActivityState, bool)\n\n// Derivers maps the agent token in `ao hooks <agent> <event>` to its deriver.\n//\n// grok, continue, and devin install Claude Code-compatible hooks whose callback\n// command is literally `ao hooks claude-code <event>`, so the native agent\n// never invokes `ao hooks grok` — but the original dispatch accepted those\n// tokens, so they are kept here (routed to the Claude deriver) to preserve that\n// behavior exactly.\nvar Derivers = map[string]DeriveFunc{\n\t\"claude-code\": claudecode.DeriveActivityState,\n\t\"grok\":        claudecode.DeriveActivityState,\n\t\"continue\":    claudecode.DeriveActivityState,\n\t\"devin\":       claudecode.DeriveActivityState,\n\t\"codex\":       codex.DeriveActivityState,\n\t\"droid\":       droid.DeriveActivityState,\n\t\"agy\":         agy.DeriveActivityState,\n\t\"cursor\":      cursor.DeriveActivityState,\n\t\"qwen\":        qwen.DeriveActivityState,\n\t\"copilot\":     copilot.DeriveActivityState,\n\t\"goose\":       goose.DeriveActivityState,\n\t\"cline\":       cline.DeriveActivityState,\n\t\"kiro\":        kiro.DeriveActivityState,\n\t\"kilocode\":    kilocode.DeriveActivityState,\n\t\"autohand\":    autohand.DeriveActivityState,\n}\n\n// Derive looks up the deriver for an agent token and applies it. ok=false when\n// the token has no registered deriver or the event carries no activity signal —\n// the caller reports nothing in either case.\nfunc Derive(agent, event string, payload []byte) (domain.ActivityState, bool) {\n\tderive, found := Derivers[agent]\n\tif !found {\n\t\treturn \"\", false\n\t}\n\treturn derive(event, payload)\n}\n"
}

{\n\t\tif tok == \"\" {\n\t\t\treturn fail(r, \"argv[%d] is an empty string: %v\", i, cmd)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tcmd2, err := ha.Agent.GetLaunchCommand(ctx, cfg)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fail(r, normalizeArgv(cmd))\n\t\t}\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn fail(r, \"GetPromptDeliveryStrategy returned invalid value %q\", strategy)\n\t}\n\n\tr.Status = StatusPass\n\tr.Detail = fmt.Sprintf(\"deterministic ```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/reverbcode/backend/internal/adapters/agent/conformance/conformance.go",
  "old_string": "// normalizeArgv replaces argv[0] (which may be an absolute, machine-specific\n// binary path resolved off PATH) with its basename, so evidence and golden\n// snapshots are stable across machines.\nfunc normalizeArgv(cmd []string) []string {\n\tif len(cmd) == 0 {\n\t\treturn cmd\n\t}\n\tout := append([]string(nil), cmd...)\n\tout[0] = filepath.Base(out[0])\n\treturn out\n}",
  "new_string": "// normalizeArgv rewrites a command so evidence and golden snapshots are stable\n// across runs and machines:\n//   - the per-run eval workspace path becomes <workspace>,\n//   - any other path under the OS temp dir becomes <tmp>/…,\n//   - any remaining absolute path (a machine-specific resolved binary, e.g.\n//     /Users/me/.local/bin/goose or a Nix profile path) becomes its basename.\n//\n// Argument values that legitimately carry a path (a worktree --cwd, a temp\n// settings file) are stabilized by the first two rules before the basename\n// rule sees them, so only real binary paths get shortened.\nfunc normalizeArgv(cmd []string, ws string) []string {\n\tif len(cmd) == 0 {\n\t\treturn cmd\n\t}\n\ttmp := strings.TrimRight(os.TempDir(), \"/\")\n\tout := make([]string, len(cmd))\n\tfor i, tok := range cmd {\n\t\tt := tok\n\t\tif ws != \"\" {\n\t\t\tt = strings.ReplaceAll(t, ws, \"<workspace>\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tif tmp != \"\" {\n\t\t\tt = strings.ReplaceAll(t, tmp, \"<tmp>\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tif filepath.IsAbs(t) {\n\t\t\tt = filepath.Base(t)\n\t\t}\n\t\tout[i] = t\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}"
}
```

  "content": "package evalrig\n\nimport (\n\t\"context\"\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"os/exec\"\n\t\"time\"\n)\n\n// Stage drives the sibling Zellij pane where demonstrations run. The control\n// deck types commands into it with `zellij action paste` + `send-keys Enter`,\n// targeting the pane by id so the deck never has to surrender focus. Discovery\n// matches the pane the layout names \"stage\" (the same title-match the runtime\n// adapter uses for its \"agent\" pane).\n//\n// Outside Zellij (Available()==false) every method is a graceful no-op, so the\n// deck still runs as a plain matrix viewer for development.\ntype Stage struct {\n\tsession string\n\tpaneID  string\n\trun     zellijRunner\n}\n\n// zellijRunner executes a `zellij` invocation; injectable so the deck can be\n// tested without a live multiplexer.\ntype zellijRunner func(ctx context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error)\n\n// paneInfo mirrors the fields the deck needs from `zellij action list-panes\n// --json` (see internal/adapters/runtime/zellij: the same shape and title match).\ntype paneInfo struct {\n\tID       int    `json:\"id\"`\n\tIsPlugin bool   `json:\"is_plugin\"`\n\tTitle    string `json:\"title\"`\n}\n\nconst (\n\tstagePaneTitle = \"stage\"\n\tdeckPaneTitle  = \"deck\"\n)\n\n// NewStage discovers the stage pane in the current Zellij session, if any.\nfunc NewStage(ctx context.Context) *Stage {\n\treturn newStage(ctx, os.Getenv(\"ZELLIJ_SESSION_NAME\"), execZellij)\n}\n\nfunc newStage(ctx context.Context, session string, run zellijRunner) *Stage {\n\ts := &Stage{session: session, run: run}\n\tif s.session != \"\" {\n\t\ts.paneID = s.discoverStagePane(ctx)\n\t}\n\treturn s\n}\n\n// Available reports whether the deck is running inside Zellij with a stage pane\n// it can drive.\nfunc (s *Stage) Available() bool { return s != nil && s.session != \"\" && s.paneID != \"\" }\n\n// PaneID returns the discovered stage pane id (empty when unavailable).\nfunc (s *Stage) PaneID() string {\n\tif s == nil {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\treturn s.paneID\n}\n\n// Run types command into the stage pane and presses Enter, so the audience\n// watches it execute live. It is a no-op when no stage is available.\nfunc (s *Stage) Run(ctx context.Context, command string) error {\n\tif !s.Available() {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif _, err := s.run(ctx, \"--session\", s.session, \"action\", \"paste\", \"--pane-id\", s.paneID, command); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"stage paste: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif _, err := s.run(ctx, \"--session\", s.session, \"action\", \"send-keys\", \"--pane-id\", s.paneID, \"Enter\"); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"stage enter: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// Clear blanks the stage pane (best effort), so each demonstration starts fresh.\nfunc (s *Stage) Clear(ctx context.Context) error {\n\treturn s.Run(ctx, \"clear\")\n}\n\nfunc (s *Stage) discoverStagePane(ctx context.Context) string {\n\tout, err := s.run(ctx, \"--session\", s.session, \"action\", \"list-panes\", \"--all\", \"--json\")\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\tvar panes []paneInfo\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(out, &panes); err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\t// Prefer the pane the layout titled \"stage\"; fall back to any non-plugin,\n\t// non-\"deck\" pane so a renamed layout still works.\n\tvar fallback string\n\tfor _, p := range panes {\n\t\tif p.IsPlugin {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif p.Title == stagePaneTitle {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"terminal_%d\", p.ID)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif p.Title != deckPaneTitle && fallback == \"\" {\n\t\t\tfallback = fmt.Sprintf(\"terminal_%d\", p.ID)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn fallback\n}\n\nfunc execZellij(ctx context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {\n\tcmdCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)\n\tdefer cancel()\n\treturn exec.CommandContext(cmdCtx, \"zellij\", args...).Output()\n}\n"
}

The verdicts\n// come from the same in-process conformance engine CI runs, so the demo and the\n// regression guard can never disagree.\npackage evalrig\n\nimport (\n\t\"context\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\n\ttea \"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea\"\n\t\"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss\"\n\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/conformance\"\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/registry\"\n)\n\ntype cellState int\n\nconst (\n\tcellPending cellState = iota\n\tcellRunning\n\tcellDone\n)\n\n// Model is the control-deck state.\ntype Model struct {\n\tharnessed []registry.HarnessAgent\n\tdims      []string\n\tstate     map[string]map[string]cellState\n\tresult    map[string]map[string]conformance.Result\n\trow, col  int\n\tlogs      []string\n\tstage     *Stage\n\twidth     int\n\tquitting  bool\n}\n\n// cellResultMsg carries a finished cell verdict back into Update.\ntype cellResultMsg struct {\n\tharness string\n\tdim     string\n\tresult  conformance.Result\n}\n\n// New builds the deck over the registered adapters and a (possibly no-op) stage.\nfunc New(stage *Stage) Model {\n\tharnessed := registry.Harnessed()\n\tstate := make(map[string]map[string]cellState, len(harnessed))\n\tresult := make(map[string]map[string]conformance.Result, len(harnessed))\n\tfor _, ha := range harnessed {\n\t\th := string(ha.Harness)\n\t\tstate[h] = map[string]cellState{}\n\t\tresult[h] = map[string]conformance.Result{}\n\t\tfor _, d := range conformance.Dimensions {\n\t\t\tstate[h][d] = cellPending\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn Model{\n\t\tharnessed: harnessed,\n\t\tdims:      conformance.Dimensions,\n\t\tstate:     state,\n\t\tresult:    result,\n\t\tstage:     stage,\n\t}\n}\n\n// Init implements tea.Model.\nfunc (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd { return nil }\n\n// Update implements tea.Model.\nfunc (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {\n\tswitch msg := msg.(type) {\n\tcase tea.WindowSizeMsg:\n\t\tm.width = msg.Width\n\t\treturn m, nil\n\n\tcase cellResultMsg:\n\t\tm.state[msg.harness][msg.dim] = cellDone\n\t\tm.result[msg.harness][msg.dim] = msg.result\n\t\tm.appendLog(fmt.Sprintf(\"%s/%s → %s\", msg.harness, msg.dim, strings.ToUpper(string(msg.result.Status))))\n\t\treturn m, nil\n\n\tcase tea.KeyMsg:\n\t\treturn m.handleKey(msg)\n\t}\n\treturn m, nil\n}\n\nfunc (m Model) handleKey(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {\n\tswitch msg.String() {\n\tcase \"q\", \"ctrl+c\", \"esc\":\n\t\tm.quitting = true\n\t\treturn m, tea.Quit\n\tcase \"up\", \"k\":\n\t\tm.row = clamp(m.row-1, 0, len(m.harnessed)-1)\n\tcase \"down\", \"j\":\n\t\tm.row = clamp(m.row+1, 0, len(m.harnessed)-1)\n\tcase \"left\", \"h\":\n\t\tm.col = clamp(m.col-1, 0, len(m.dims)-1)\n\tcase \"right\", \"l\":\n\t\tm.col = clamp(m.col+1, 0, len(m.dims)-1)\n\tcase \"enter\":\n\t\t// Run the selected cell, then advance to the next — the \"keep pressing\n\t\t// enter to run the next test\" presenter flow.\n\t\tcmd := m.runSelected()\n\t\tm.advance()\n\t\treturn m, cmd\n\tcase \" \", \"r\":\n\t\treturn m, m.runSelected()\n\tcase \"a\":\n\t\t// Run every dimension for the current adapter.\n\t\treturn m, m.runRow(m.row)\n\tcase \"A\":\n\t\t// Run the whole matrix.\n\t\treturn m, m.runAll()\n\t}\n\treturn m, nil\n}\n\nfunc (m *Model) runSelected() tea.Cmd {\n\treturn m.runCell(m.row, m.col)\n}\n\nfunc (m *Model) runCell(row, col int) tea.Cmd {\n\tha := m.harnessed[row]\n\th := string(ha.Harness)\n\tdim := m.dims[col]\n\tif m.state[h][dim] == cellRunning {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tm.state[h][dim] = cellRunning\n\tm.appendLog(fmt.Sprintf(\"running %s/%s …\", h, dim))\n\tstage := m.stage\n\treturn func() tea.Msg {\n\t\tctx := context.Background()\n\t\t// Show the real test executing on stage (best effort), then compute the\n\t\t// authoritative verdict in-process.\n\t\t_ = stage.Run(ctx, goTestCommand(h, dim))\n\t\tres, _ := conformance.RunDimension(ctx, ha, dim)\n\t\treturn cellResultMsg{harness: h, dim: dim, result: res}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (m *Model) runRow(row int) tea.Cmd {\n\tcmds := make([]tea.Cmd, 0, len(m.dims))\n\tfor c := range m.dims {\n\t\tif cmd := m.runCell(row, c); cmd != nil {\n\t\t\tcmds = append(cmds, cmd)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn tea.Batch(cmds...)\n}\n\nfunc (m *Model) runAll() tea.Cmd {\n\tcmds := make([]tea.Cmd, 0, len(m.harnessed)*len(m.dims))\n\tfor r := range m.harnessed {\n\t\tfor c := range m.dims {\n\t\t\tif cmd := m.runCell(r, c); cmd != nil {\n\t\t\t\tcmds = append(cmds, cmd)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn tea.Batch(cmds...)\n}\n\n// advance moves the cursor to the next cell, left-to-right then down a row.\nfunc (m *Model) advance() {\n\tm.col++\n\tif m.col >= len(m.dims) {\n\t\tm.col = 0\n\t\tif m.row < len(m.harnessed)-1 {\n\t\t\tm.row++\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tm.col = len(m.dims) - 1 // stay on the last cell\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (m *Model) appendLog(line string) {\n\tm.logs = append(m.logs, line)\n\tif len(m.logs) > 6 {\n\t\tm.logs = m.logs[len(m.logs)-6:]\n\t}\n}\n\n// goTestCommand is the command the stage runs to demonstrate one cell: the real\n// conformance subtest, in verbose mode, so the audience sees genuine PASS lines.\nfunc goTestCommand(harness, dim string) string {\n\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\n\t\t\"go test ./internal/adapters/agent/conformance/ -run 'TestConformance/%s/%s' -v -count=1\",\n\t\tharness, dim,\n\t)\n}\n\nfunc clamp(v, lo, hi int) int {\n\tif v < lo {\n\t\treturn lo\n\t}\n\tif v > hi {\n\t\treturn hi\n\t}\n\treturn v\n}\n"
}

16\n\tdimW     = 6\n)\n\nvar (\n\tcolGreen  = lipgloss.Color(\"42\")\n\tcolRed    = lipgloss.Color(\"203\")\n\tcolOrange = lipgloss.Color(\"214\")\n\tcolYellow = lipgloss.Color(\"220\")\n\tcolGray   = \"SPAWN\",\n\tconformance.DimActivity:    \"ACT\",\n\tconformance.DimSessionInfo: \"INFO\",\n\tconformance.DimPermissions: \"PERM\",\n\tconformance.DimHooks:       \"HOOK\",\n\tconformance.DimCommands:    \"CMD\",\n}\n\n// View implements tea.Model.\nfunc (m Model) View() string {\n\tif m.quitting {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\tvar b string(ha.Harness)\n\t\tnameStyle := harnessStyle\n\t\tif r == m.row {\n\t\t\tnameStyle = harnessSel\n\t\t}\n\t\tb.WriteString(nameStyle.Width(harnessW).Render(truncate(h, harnessW-1)))\n\t\tfor c, d all · ↑↓←→ / hjkl move · q quit\"))\n\tb.WriteString(\"\\n\")\n\treturn b.String()\n}\n\nfunc (m Model) detailPanel() string {\n\tha := m.harnessed[m.row]\n\th := string(ha.Harness)\n\td := m.dims[m.col]\n\ttitle := fmt.Sprintf(\"▸ %s / %s\", h, d)\n\n\tswitch m.state[h][d] {\n\tcase cellRunning:\n\t\treturn panelStyle.Render(title + \"   \" + \"\\n\"))\n\tdefault: // cellPending\n\t\treturn panelStyle.Render(title + \"   \" + lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(colDim).Render(\"(not run)\") +\n\t\t\t\"\\n\" + lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(colDim).Render(goTestCommand(h, d)))\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc renderCell(state cellState, status conformance.Status, selected bool) string {\n\tglyph, col := cellGlyph(state, status)\n\ts := lipgloss.NewStyle().Width(dimW).Align(lipgloss.Center).Foreground(col)\n\tif selected {\n\t\ts = s.Reverse(true).Bold(true)\n\t}\n\treturn s.Render(glyph)\n}\n\nfunc cellGlyph(state cellState, status conformance.Status) (string, lipgloss.Color) {\n\tswitch state {\n\tcase cellRunning:\n\t\treturn \"•\", colYellow\n\tcase cellDone:\n\t\tswitch status {\n\t\tcase conformance.StatusPass:\n\t\t\treturn \"✓\", colGreen\n\t\tcase conformance.StatusFail:\n\t\t\treturn \"✗\", colRed\n\t\tcase conformance.StatusGap:\n\t\t\treturn \"▲\", colOrange\n\t\tcase conformance.StatusSkip:\n\t\t\treturn \"–\", colDim\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn \"·\", colDim\n}\n\nfunc statusBadge(status conformance.Status) string {\n\tcol := colDim\n\tswitch status {\n\tcase conformance.StatusPass:\n\t\tcol = colGreen\n\tcase conformance.StatusFail:\n\t\tcol = colRed\n\tcase conformance.StatusGap:\n\t\tcol = colOrange\n\tcase conformance.StatusSkip:\n\t\tcol = colGray\n\t}\n\treturn lipgloss.NewStyle().Bold(true).Foreground(col).Render(strings.ToUpper(string(status)))\n}\n\nfunc stageBadge(s *Stage) string {\n\tif s.Available() {\n\t\treturn lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(colGreen).Render(\"● stage: \"+s.PaneID())\n\t}\n\treturn lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(colDim).Render(\"○ stage: none (matrix-only)\")\n}\n\nfunc truncate(s string, max int) string {\n\tif max <= 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\tr := []rune(s)\n\tif len(r) <= max {\n\t\treturn s\n\t}\n\tif max == 1 {\n\t\treturn \"…\"\n\t}\n\treturn string(r[:max-1]) + \"…\"\n}\n"

  "content": "package evalrig\n\nimport (\n\t\"context\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"testing\"\n\n\ttea \"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea\"\n\n\t\"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/conformance\"\n)\n\n// fakeZellij records the args of every zellij invocation and answers list-panes\n// with a fixed JSON payload.\ntype fakeZellij struct {\n\tlistJSON string\n\tcalls    [][]string\n}\n\nfunc (f *fakeZellij) run(_ context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {\n\tf.calls = append(f.calls, args)\n\tif len(args) >= 4 && args[3] == \"list-panes\" {\n\t\treturn []byte(f.listJSON), nil\n\t}\n\treturn nil, nil\n}\n\nfunc TestStageDiscoversPaneByTitle(t *testing.T) {\n\tf := &fakeZellij{listJSON: `[\n\t\t{\"id\":0,\"is_plugin\":false,\"title\":\"deck\"},\n\t\t{\"id\":1,\"is_plugin\":true,\"title\":\"stage\"},\n\t\t{\"id\":2,\"is_plugin\":false,\"title\":\"stage\"}\n\t]`}\n\ts := newStage(context.Background(), \"sess-1\", f.run)\n\tif !s.Available() {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"Available() = false, want true\")\n\t}\n\t// The non-plugin \"stage\" pane (id 2) wins over the plugin one (id 1).\n\tif s.PaneID() != \"terminal_2\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"PaneID() = %q, want terminal_2\", s.PaneID())\n\t}\n\n\tif err := s.Run(context.Background(), \"go test ./...\"); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"Run: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\t// Last two calls must be a paste of the command, then an Enter, both\n\t// targeting the discovered pane id.\n\tpaste := s.lastCallWith(f, \"paste\")\n\tif paste == nil || paste[len(paste)-1] != \"go test ./...\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"paste call = %v\", paste)\n\t}\n\tif !contains(paste, \"--pane-id\") || !contains(paste, \"terminal_2\") {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"paste did not target the stage pane: %v\", paste)\n\t}\n\tenter := s.lastCallWith(f, \"send-keys\")\n\tif enter == nil || enter[len(enter)-1] != \"Enter\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"send-keys call = %v\", enter)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestStageFallsBackToNonDeckPane(t *testing.T) {\n\t// No pane titled \"stage\": fall back to the first non-plugin, non-deck pane.\n\tf := &fakeZellij{listJSON: `[\n\t\t{\"id\":0,\"is_plugin\":false,\"title\":\"deck\"},\n\t\t{\"id\":7,\"is_plugin\":false,\"title\":\"scratch\"}\n\t]`}\n\ts := newStage(context.Background(), \"sess-1\", f.run)\n\tif s.PaneID() != \"terminal_7\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"PaneID() = %q, want terminal_7 (fallback)\", s.PaneID())\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestStageNoopWithoutSession(t *testing.T) {\n\tf := &fakeZellij{}\n\ts := newStage(context.Background(), \"\", f.run)\n\tif s.Available() {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"Available() = true without a session\")\n\t}\n\tif err := s.Run(context.Background(), \"echo hi\"); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"Run no-op: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\tif len(f.calls) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"expected no zellij calls without a session, got %v\", f.calls)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (s *Stage) lastCallWith(f *fakeZellij, action string) []string {\n\tvar found []string\n\tfor _, c := range f.calls {\n\t\tif len(c) >= 4 && c[3] == action {\n\t\t\tfound = c\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn found\n}\n\nfunc contains(ss []string, want string) bool {\n\tfor _, s := range ss {\n\t\tif s == want {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\n// noopStage is a Stage that is never \"available\", so the deck runs matrix-only.\nfunc noopStage() *Stage { return &Stage{} }\n\nfunc TestModelRunCellComputesVerdict(t *testing.T) {\n\tm := New(noopStage())\n\tif len(m.harnessed) == 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"no adapters\")\n\t}\n\t// Default cursor is the first adapter / first dimension (spawn). Pressing\n\t// enter runs that cell and advances the cursor.\n\tupdated, cmd := m.Update(tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyEnter})\n\tm = updated.(Model)\n\tif cmd == nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"enter produced no command\")\n\t}\n\th := string(m.harnessed[0].Harness)\n\tif m.state[h][conformance.DimSpawn] != cellRunning {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"selected cell state = %v, want running\", m.state[h][conformance.DimSpawn])\n\t}\n\tif m.col != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"cursor did not advance: col = %d, want 1\", m.col)\n\t}\n\n\t// Execute the command to get the verdict, then feed it back.\n\tmsg := cmd()\n\tres, ok := msg.(cellResultMsg)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"command returned %T, want cellResultMsg\", msg)\n\t}\n\tupdated, _ = m.Update(res)\n\tm = updated.(Model)\n\tif m.state[h][conformance.DimSpawn] != cellDone {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"cell state after result = %v, want done\", m.state[h][conformance.DimSpawn])\n\t}\n\tif got := m.result[h][conformance.DimSpawn].Status; got != conformance.StatusPass {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"spawn verdict = %q, want pass\", got)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestModelNavigationClamps(t *testing.T) {\n\tm := New(noopStage())\n\t// Up/left at the origin must not go negative.\n\tup, _ := m.Update(tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyUp})\n\tleft, _ := up.(Model).Update(tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyLeft})\n\tm = left.(Model)\n\tif m.row != 0 || m.col != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"clamp failed: row=%d col=%d\", m.row, m.col)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestModelViewRenders(t *testing.T) {\n\tm := New(noopStage())\n\tout := m.View()\n\tfor _, want := range []string{\"AO Adapter Proving Ground\", \"HARNESS\", \"SPAWN\", string(m.harnessed[0].Harness), \"matrix-only\"} {\n\t\tif !strings.Contains(stripANSI(out), want) {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"view missing %q\\n---\\n%s\", want, stripANSI(out))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// stripANSI removes ANSI escape sequences so assertions match the visible text.\nfunc stripANSI(s string) string {\n\tvar b strings.Builder\n\tinEsc := false\n\tfor i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {\n\t\tc := s[i]\n\t\tif c == 0x1b {\n\t\t\tinEsc = true\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif inEsc {\n\t\t\tif (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') {\n\t\t\t\tinEsc = false\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tb.WriteByte(c)\n\t}\n\treturn b.String()\n}\n"
}

{

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n#\n# demo.sh — launch the AO Adapter Proving Ground (or record it).\n#\n#   ./demo.sh              # interactive two-pane demo in Zellij\n#   ./demo.sh --record     # same, captured to evalrig.cast with asciinema\n#   ./demo.sh --record out.cast\n#\n# The deck (left) is `ao evalrig`; the stage (right) is a shell the deck drives\n# to run the real `go test` for each cell. Quit the deck with `q`, then exit\n# Zellij to stop a recording.\nset -euo pipefail\n\nhere=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\nrepo=\"$(cd \"$here/../..\" && pwd)\"\nbackend=\"$repo/backend\"\nlayout=\"$here/evalrig.kdl\"\n\nfor bin in zellij go; do\n    command -v \"$bin\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo \"demo.sh: '$bin' not found in PATH\" >&2; exit 1; }\ndone\n\necho \"Building ao …\"\n( cd \"$backend\" && go build -o \"$backend/bin/ao\" ./cmd/ao )\n\n# The deck pane runs `ao` (must be on PATH); the stage runs go test from backend/.\nexport PATH=\"$backend/bin:$PATH\"\ncd \"$backend\"\n\nsession=\"evalrig-$$\"\nlaunch=( zellij --session \"$session\" --layout \"$layout\" )\n\nif [[ \"${1:-}\" == \"--record\" ]]; then\n    command -v asciinema >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo \"demo.sh: asciinema not found\" >&2; exit 1; }\n    cast=\"${2:-$here/evalrig.cast}\"\n    echo \"Recording to $cast …\"\n    exec asciinema rec --overwrite -c \"${launch[*]}\" \"$cast\"\nfi\n\nexec \"${launch[@]}\"\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/reverbcode/test/evalrig/README.md",
  "content": "# AO Adapter Proving Ground\n\nAn interactive, recordable demonstration that every agent adapter is tested\nalong the six dimensions we verify by hand:\n\n| # | Dimension | What it proves |\n|---|-----------|----------------|\n| 1 | **spawn** | the launch command is well-formed, deterministic, and matches the declared prompt-delivery strategy |\n| 2 | **activity** | the hooks the adapter installs are actually dispatched (`ao hooks <tok>` has a deriver) |\n| 3 | **sessioninfo** | title/summary/id are derived from metadata only — never by reading transcripts |\n| 4 | **permissions** | `default` emits no flag; each non-default mode maps to a distinct, real flag |\n| 5 | **hooks** | install is idempotent and writes a worktree-local (non-tracked) config |\n| 6 | **commands** | the exact launch/restore argv, snapshotted for review against each agent's CLI docs |\n\nThe verdicts come from the in-process conformance engine in\n`backend/internal/adapters/agent/conformance` — the *same code CI runs* — so the\ndemo and the regression guard can never disagree.\n\n## The two surfaces\n\n- **Control deck** (`ao evalrig`) — a Bubble Tea TUI rendering the\n  adapters × dimensions matrix. The presenter runs cells one keypress at a time.\n- **Stage** — a sibling Zellij pane the deck drives (via `zellij action paste`)\n  to run the real `go test` for each selected cell, so an audience watches\n  genuine PASS lines while the matrix cell fills in.\n\n```\n┌─ deck (ao evalrig) ───────────┬─ stage (go test live) ─────────┐\n│ HARNESS     SPAWN ACT INFO …  │ $ go test … -run …/spawn -v    │\n│ claude-code   ✓    ✓   ✓  …   │ === RUN   TestConformance/…     │\n│▸opencode      ✓    ▲   ✓  …   │ --- PASS: …                     │\n│ …                             │                                 │\n└───────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\nLegend: `✓` pass · `▲` gap (wired-but-broken) · `✗` fail (contract violation) ·\n`–` n/a (adapter limitation) · `·` not run yet.\n\n## Run it\n\n```bash\n# Interactive two-pane demo (Zellij). Requires: zellij, go.\ntest/evalrig/demo.sh\n```\n\nKeys: `enter` run+advance · `space`/`r` re-run · `a` run row · `A` run all ·\narrows / `hjkl` move · `q` quit.\n\nRun the deck alone (matrix-only, no stage) from anywhere:\n\n```bash\ncd backend && go run ./cmd/ao evalrig\n```\n\n## Record it\n\n```bash\n# Live, presenter-paced capture (terminal-native .cast). Requires: asciinema.\ntest/evalrig/demo.sh --record            # -> test/evalrig/evalrig.cast\nasciinema play test/evalrig/evalrig.cast\n\n# Deterministic, embeddable GIF trailer (matrix-only). Requires: vhs.\ncd test/evalrig && vhs evalrig.tape      # -> evalrig.gif\n```\n\nUse **asciinema** to prove you drove it live at your own pace; use **VHS** to\nregenerate a clean GIF for a README/Slack/PR. Both reuse the same deck — they're\nrecorders, not separate rigs.\n\n## The engine underneath (run without the TUI)\n\n```bash\ncd backend\n\n# The full matrix + per-cell detail, as text (report-only):\ngo test ./internal/adapters/agent/conformance/ -run TestConformance -v\n\n# One cell:\ngo test ./internal/adapters/agent/conformance/ -run 'TestConformance/opencode/activity' -v\n\n# Turn it into an enforcing CI gate (fail on FAIL/GAP and golden drift):\nAOEVAL_STRICT=1 go test ./internal/adapters/agent/conformance/...\n\n# Regenerate the golden command snapshots + matrix.txt after an intended change:\nAOEVAL_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/adapters/agent/conformance/...\n```\n\nGolden launch/restore commands live in\n`backend/internal/adapters/agent/conformance/testdata/golden/<harness>.txt`.\n\n## Adding a new adapter\n\nA new harness is registered in one place —\n`backend/internal/adapters/agent/registry` (`Constructors`) — and, if it reports\nactivity, mapped in `backend/internal/adapters/agent/activitydispatch`\n(`Derivers`). The proving ground picks it up automatically; the conformance\nsuite will immediately show its row.\n"
}

Phases 1, 2, and 4 are **complete and validated end-to-end**. Here's where things stand.

## What's built and proven

**The engine** (`internal/adapters/agent/conformance`) — the eval-matrix-as-code: 23 adapters × 6 dimensions, all in-process, zero agent binaries, deterministic. Report-only by default; `AOEVAL_STRICT=1` makes it a CI gate. It already surfaces real findings:
- **opencode** — Activity **GAP**: installs `ao hooks opencode` callbacks that nothing dispatches → activity silently dropped.
- A clean limitation map (`amp/aider/auggie/kimi/vibe/pi/crush` are spawn+commands-only).
- 23 machine-stable **golden command snapshots** for dimension-#6 review against each agent's real CLI docs.

**The refactors** (behavior-preserving, 0 new lint): a shared `registry` package and an `activitydispatch` table — both the daemon and `cli/hooks.go` now delegate, so a new harness is one edit and the rig picks it up automatically.

**The control deck** (`ao evalrig`) — a Bubble Tea TUI: the matrix grid, presenter-paced **enter = run + advance**, a detail panel (showing e.g. the opencode GAP explanation), and a live stage badge. Unit-tested, lint-clean.

**The Zellij + recording layer** (`test/evalrig/`) — `evalrig.kdl` (deck + stage), `demo.sh` (asciinema), `evalrig.tape` (VHS GIF), README. I validated the whole choreography **against real Zellij headlessly**: layout parses, deck/stage panes resolve by title, and a pasted command actually executes on the stage (`AOEVAL_STAGE_OK_42`).

## You can run it right now

```bash

test/evalrig/demo.sh --record   # + asciinema capture
cd backend && go run ./cmd/ao evalrig   # matrix-only, no Zellij
```

(The one failing repo test, `TestSessionStreamsRealZellijPane`, is a pre-existing macOS `$TMPDIR` socket-length issue, unrelated to my changes.) Everything is uncommitted.

## The one remaining piece — Phase 3 (live mode)

The deterministic rig fully satisfies "prove to the org" on any machine. Phase 3 adds the *hybrid wow*: live `ao spawn` of an installed agent into the stage, polling `GET /sessions/{id}` to show real activity (`active→idle→waiting_input`) and SessionInfo filling in. It needs a running daemon, a registered project, and the agent's binary — heavier, and its demo value depends on what you have installed.

The\n// `ao evalrig` command wires it over the shared CLI client; defining it here\n// keeps the evalrig package free of a dependency on the cli package.\ntype DaemonClient interface {\n\tGet(ctx context.Context, path string, out any) error\n\tPost(ctx context.Context, path string, body, out any) error\n}\n\n// LiveConfig enables live spawns. Live mode is off unless both a client and a\n// project are supplied (and a daemon is actually reachable, which surfaces as a\n// spawn error if not).\ntype LiveConfig struct {\n\tClient    DaemonClient\n\tProjectID string\n\tPrompt    string\n}\n\nfunc (l LiveConfig) enabled() bool { return l.Client != nil && l.ProjectID != \"\" }\n\n// liveSession is the deck's view of a real, daemon-managed session it spawned.\ntype liveSession struct {\n\tid          string\n\tharness     string\n\tstate       string\n\tdisplayName string\n\tstatus      string\n\tterminated  bool\n\terrText     string\n\thistory     []string\n}\n\n// --- wire DTOs (mirrored, per AGENTS.md, so evalrig need not import httpd) ---\n\ntype liveSpawnRequest struct {\n\tProjectID string `json:\"id\"`\n\t\tStatus string `json:\"status\"`\n\t} `json:\"session\"`\n}\n\ntype liveSessionDTO struct {\n\tID           string `json:\"id\"`\n\tHarness      string `json:\"harness\"`\n\tDisplayName  string `json:\"displayName\"`\n\tIsTerminated bool   `json:\"isTerminated\"`\n\tStatus       string `json:\"status\"`\n\tActivity     struct {\n\t\tState string `json:\"state\"`\n\t} `json:\"activity\"`\n}\n\ntype liveSessionResponse struct {\n\tSession liveSessionDTO `json:\"session\"`\n}\n\n// --- messages ---\n\ntype liveSpawnResultMsg struct {\n\tharness string\n\tid      string\n\tstatus  string\n\terr     error\n}\n\ntype livePollResultMsg struct {\n\tid  string\n\tdto liveSessionDTO\n\terr error\n}\n\ntype livePollTickMsg struct{ id string }\n\n// --- behavior ---\n\n// startLive spawns the selected adapter as a real session and begins polling,\n// or logs why it can't (live disabled, or the agent's binary isn't installed).\nfunc (m *Model) startLive() tea.Cmd {\n\tha := m.harnessed[m.row]\n\th := string(ha.Harness)\n\n\tif !m.live.enabled() {\n\t\tm.appendLog(\"live: needs --project <id> and a running daemon (ao start)\")\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif !m.capable(ha) {\n\t\tm.appendLog(fmt.Sprintf(\"live: %s binary not installed — deterministic only\", h))\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tm.appendLog(fmt.Sprintf(\"live: spawning %s …\", h))\n\t_ = m.stage.Run(context.Background(),\n\t\tfmt.Sprintf(\"# live: ao spawn --project %s --harness %s\", m.live.ProjectID, h))\n\n\tclient := m.live.Client\n\treq := liveSpawnRequest{ProjectID: m.live.ProjectID, Harness: h, Prompt: m.live.Prompt}\n\treturn func() tea.Msg {\n\t\tvar res liveSpawnResponse\n\t\terr := client.Post(context.Background(), \"sessions\", req, &res)\n\t\treturn liveSpawnResultMsg{harness: h, id: res.Session.ID, status: res.Session.Status, err: err}\n\t}\n}\n\n// pollCmd reads the live session's current state once.\nfunc (m *Model) pollCmd(id string) tea.Cmd {\n\tclient := m.live.Client\n\treturn func() tea.Msg {\n\t\tvar res liveSessionResponse\n\t\terr := client.Get(context.Background(), \"sessions/\"+url.PathEscape(id), &res)\n\t\treturn livePollResultMsg{id: id, dto: res.Session, err: err}\n\t}\n}\n\n// applyLiveSpawn handles the spawn result and kicks off polling.\nfunc (m *Model) applyLiveSpawn(msg liveSpawnResultMsg) tea.Cmd {\n\tif msg.err != nil {\n\t\tm.appendLog(fmt.Sprintf(\"live: spawn %s failed: %v\", msg.harness, msg.err))\n\t\tm.liveSession = nil\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tm.liveSession = &liveSession{id: msg.id, harness: msg.harness, status: msg.status, state: \"…\"}\n\tm.appendLog(fmt.Sprintf(\"live: %s spawned as %s\", msg.harness, msg.id))\n\treturn m.pollCmd(msg.id)\n}\n\n// applyLivePoll updates the live session and schedules the next poll until the\n// session terminates or errors.\nfunc (m *Model) applyLivePoll(msg livePollResultMsg) tea.Cmd {\n\tif m.liveSession == nil || m.liveSession.id != msg.id {\n\t\treturn nil // a stale poll for a session the presenter already cleared.\n\t}\n\tif msg.err != nil {\n\t\tm.liveSession.errText = msg.err.Error()\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tls := m.liveSession\n\tif msg.dto.State() != \"\" && msg.dto.State() != ls.state {\n\t\tls.history = append(ls.history, msg.dto.State())\n\t\tif len(ls.history) > 8 {\n\t\t\tls.history = ls.history[len(ls.history)-8:]\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tls.state = msg.dto.State()\n\tls.displayName = msg.dto.DisplayName\n\tls.status = msg.dto.Status\n\tls.terminated = msg.dto.IsTerminated\n\tif ls.terminated || ls.state == string(ports.PermissionModeDefault) /*never*/ {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif ls.terminated {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tid := ls.id\n\treturn tea.Tick(pollInterval, func(time.Time) tea.Msg { return livePollTickMsg{id: id} })\n}\n\n// State returns the activity state, defaulting to empty.\nfunc (d liveSessionDTO) State() string { return d.Activity.State }\n\n// capable reports (and caches) whether an adapter's native binary is installed,\n// so live spawn isn't offered for an agent that can't run here.\nfunc (m *Model) capable(ha registry.HarnessAgent) bool {\n\th := string(ha.Harness)\n\tif v, ok := m.liveCap[h]; ok {\n\t\treturn v\n\t}\n\tv := binaryInstalled(context.Background(), ha)\n\tm.liveCap[h] = v\n\treturn v\n}\n\n// binaryInstalled builds the adapter's launch command and checks whether its\n// resolved binary exists — reusing GetLaunchCommand so the check needs no\n// per-adapter knowledge of the binary name.\nfunc binaryInstalled(ctx context.Context, ha registry.HarnessAgent) bool {\n\tws, err := os.MkdirTemp(\"\", \"aoeval-live-\")\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tdefer func() { _ = os.RemoveAll(ws) }()\n\n\tcmd, err := ha.Agent.GetLaunchCommand(ctx, ports.LaunchConfig{\n\t\tPermissions:   ports.PermissionModeDefault,\n\t\tPrompt:        \"x\",\n\t\tSessionID:     \"x\",\n\t\tWorkspacePath: ws,\n\t})\n\tif err != nil || len(cmd) == 0 {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tbin := cmd[0]\n\tif filepath.IsAbs(bin) {\n\t\tinfo, err := os.Stat(bin)\n\t\treturn err == nil && !info.IsDir()\n\t}\n\t_, err = With --project (and a running\n// daemon) the deck can also live-spawn an installed agent and watch its real\n// activity and session info. Run it directly for a matrix-only viewer.\nfunc newEvalRigCommand(ctx *commandContext) *cobra.Command {\n\tvar (\n\t\tproject string\n\t\tprompt  string\n\t)\n\tcmd := &cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse:   \"evalrig\",\n\t\tShort: \"Interactive adapter proving ground (eval matrix demo)\",\n\t\tLong: \"Interactive, presenter-paced demonstration of the agent adapter \" +\n\t\t\t\"conformance matrix.\\n\\n\" +\n\t\t\t\"Each cell is one (adapter, dimension) check from the same engine CI \" +\n\t\t\t\"runs. With --project and a running daemon, press L to live-spawn the \" +\n\t\t\t\"selected agent and watch its real activity. See test/evalrig/ for the \" +\n\t\t\t\"layout and recording scripts.\",\n\t\tArgs: cobra.NoArgs,\n\t\tRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {\n\t\t\tstage := evalrig.NewStage(cmd.Context())\n\t\t\tlive := evalrig.LiveConfig{Prompt: prompt}\n\t\t\tif project != \"\" {\n\t\t\t\tlive.Client = daemonClientAdapter{ctx: ctx}\n\t\t\t\tlive.ProjectID = project\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tprogram := tea.NewProgram(evalrig.New(stage, live), tea.WithAltScreen())\n\t\t\t_, err := program.Run()\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tf := cmd.Flags()\n\tf.StringVar(&project, \"project\", \"\", \"Project id for live spawns (enables the L key; requires a running daemon)\")\n\tf.StringVar(&prompt, \"prompt\", \"Add a health check endpoint and a test for it.\", \"Prompt used for live spawns\")\n\treturn cmd\n}\n"
}

## Done — the AO Adapter Proving Ground is built, tested, and validated end-to-end

**Phase 1 — Engine** (`internal/adapters/agent/conformance`): the eval-matrix-as-code. 23 adapters × 6 dimensions, in-process, hermetic, deterministic. Report-only by default; `AOEVAL_STRICT=1` makes it a CI gate. 23 machine-stable golden command snapshots. **Refactors** (behavior-preserving, 0 new lint): shared `registry` + `activitydispatch` table; daemon and `cli/hooks.go` delegate to them.

**Phase 2 — Control deck** (`ao evalrig`): Bubble Tea TUI — the matrix grid, presenter-paced **enter = run + advance**, detail panel, and Zellij stage choreography (validated against real Zellij: panes discovered by title, pasted commands execute on stage).

**Phase 3 — Live mode**: `ao evalrig --project <id>` + `L` spawns an installed agent via the daemon and a live panel shows its real activity (`active → idle → waiting_input → exited`) and hook-derived title. Auto-detects which binaries you have; degrades gracefully otherwise.

**Phase 4 — Recording** (`test/evalrig/`): `evalrig.kdl` (deck+stage), `demo.sh` (asciinema), `evalrig.tape` (VHS GIF), README, gitignore.

> AGENT

That's the nesting problem — you ran `demo.sh` **from inside an existing Zellij session** (`reverbcode`). When Zellij sees `--session <new-name>` from within a session, it interprets it as "attach to that session" (which doesn't exist) instead of "create a new one" — hence "not found".

Two real bugs in `demo.sh`:
1. It doesn't detect that you're already inside Zellij → should open a **new tab** in your current session, not a nested session.
2. A new tab (or nested session) inherits the Zellij *server's* env, so the `PATH`/`cwd` exports in `demo.sh` don't reach the panes — `ao` wouldn't be found and the stage wouldn't be in `backend/`.

Let me fix both: detect Zellij and use `new-tab`, and generate a **self-sufficient layout with absolute paths** so it works regardless of inherited env. First let me confirm the `new-tab` action and that an absolute-path layout parses:

{
  "file_path": "/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/reverbcode/test/evalrig/demo.sh",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n#\n# demo.sh — launch the AO Adapter Proving Ground (or record it).\n#\n#   ./demo.sh              # interactive deck + stage\n#   ./demo.sh --record     # same, captured to evalrig.cast with asciinema\n#   ./demo.sh --record out.cast\n#\n# Works whether or not you're already inside Zellij:\n#   - outside Zellij  -> starts a new Zellij session with the layout.\n#   - inside Zellij   -> opens the demo as a new TAB in your current session\n#                        (nesting a new session is what Zellij refuses).\n#\n# The deck (left) is `ao evalrig`; the stage (right) is a shell the deck drives\n# to run the real `go test` for each cell. Quit the deck with `q`.\nset -euo pipefail\n\nhere=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\nrepo=\"$(cd \"$here/../..\" && pwd)\"\nbackend=\"$repo/backend\"\n\nfor bin in zellij go; do\n    command -v \"$bin\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo \"demo.sh: '$bin' not found in PATH\" >&2; exit 1; }\ndone\n\necho \"Building ao …\"\n( cd \"$backend\" && go build -o \"$backend/bin/ao\" ./cmd/ao )\nao_bin=\"$backend/bin/ao\"\n\n# A resolved layout with absolute paths. Panes inherit the Zellij *server*\n# environment, not this script's, so a relative cwd or a PATH export here would\n# not reach them — bake the absolute binary path and cwd into the layout.\nlayout=\"$here/.evalrig.local.kdl\"\ncat > \"$layout\" <<KDL\nlayout {\n    cwd \"$backend\"\n    pane split_direction=\"vertical\" {\n        pane name=\"deck\" size=\"58%\" command=\"$ao_bin\" {\n            args \"evalrig\"\n        }\n        pane name=\"stage\" size=\"42%\"\n    }\n}\nKDL\n\nrecord=0\ncast=\"$here/evalrig.cast\"\nif [[ \"${1:-}\" == \"--record\" ]]; then\n    record=1\n    [[ -n \"${2:-}\" ]] && cast=\"$2\"\nfi\n\n# Already inside Zellij: open a new tab rather than nesting a session.\nif [[ -n \"${ZELLIJ:-}\" ]]; then\n    if [[ \"$record\" == 1 ]]; then\n        echo \"Note: --record must run from OUTSIDE Zellij (asciinema needs to own the session).\" >&2\n        echo \"Opening the demo in a new tab instead — record your terminal separately.\" >&2\n    fi\n    echo \"Inside Zellij → opening the proving ground in a new tab (switch tabs to see it).\"\n    exec zellij action new-tab --layout \"$layout\" --name evalrig\nfi\n\n# Fresh terminal: start a new named session with the layout.\nsession=\"evalrig-$$\"\nif [[ \"$record\" == 1 ]]; then\n    command -v asciinema >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo \"demo.sh: asciinema not found\" >&2; exit 1; }\n    echo \"Recording to $cast …\"\n    exec asciinema rec --overwrite -c \"zellij --session '$session' --layout '$layout'\" \"$cast\"\nfi\nexec zellij --session \"$session\" --layout \"$layout\"\n"
}

## What happened

You ran `demo.sh` **from inside your existing Zellij session** (`reverbcode`). When Zellij gets `--session evalrig-96217` from *within* a session, it reads it as "**attach** to that session" — which doesn't exist — instead of "create a new one." Hence `Session 'evalrig-96217' not found. ...active: reverbcode`. (Zellij doesn't nest sessions.)

## What I fixed in `demo.sh`

1. **Detects you're inside Zellij** → opens the demo as a **new tab** (`zellij action new-tab`) in your current session instead of nesting.
2. **Generates a layout with absolute paths** (`ao` binary + `backend/` cwd) — because tab/session panes inherit the Zellij *server's* environment, not the script's, so the old relative `cwd` + `PATH` export never reached them.

I validated the whole inside-Zellij path end-to-end: running the actual script with Zellij set added a tab named **`evalrig`** with the `deck` + `stage` panes (and confirmed `new-tab --layout` accepts the layout — the earlier failure mode was an unrelated inline-KDL quirk I checked against).

## What was wrong

Your deck was working perfectly (claude-code all ✓ — those verdicts come from the in-process engine, independent of the stage). The **stage** pane was the issue: it opened in the **repo root** (`/Users/.../reverbcode`), inherited from your Zellij session's cwd, but `go.mod` lives in `backend/` — so `go test ./internal/...` hit *"cannot find main module."*

A new tab inherits the **session's** working directory, and a **layout-level `cwd` doesn't override it** — I'd only verified the panes appeared, not their cwd. The fix: set `cwd` **per-pane** in the generated layout (verified: the stage's `pwd` is now `.../backend`, and the real `go test` passes there).

## What changed

`demo.sh` now passes the two-pane layout to Zellij **inline** (`--layout-string`) instead of generating `.evalrig.local.kdl`:
- **Inside Zellij** → `zellij action new-tab --layout-string … --name evalrig`
- **Outside** → `zellij --session … --layout-string …`

  "new_string": "func (m *Model) runSelected() tea.Cmd {\n\t// A deliberate single-cell run drives the stage so the audience watches the\n\t// real test execute.\n\treturn m.runCell(m.row, m.col, true)\n}\n\n// runCell runs one (adapter, dimension) check in-process. When showStage is\n// true it also types the matching `go test` into the stage pane. Bulk runs pass\n// false: typing dozens of commands into one shell would both flood it and — even\n// serialized — queue behind each other, so they only update the matrix.\nfunc (m *Model) runCell(row, col int, showStage bool) tea.Cmd {\n\tha := m.harnessed[row]\n\th := string(ha.Harness)\n\tdim := m.dims[col]\n\tif m.state[h][dim] == cellRunning {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tm.state[h][dim] = cellRunning\n\tm.appendLog(fmt.Sprintf(\"running %s/%s …\", h, dim))\n\tstage := m.stage\n\treturn func() tea.Msg {\n\t\tctx := context.Background()\n\t\tif showStage {\n\t\t\t_ = stage.Run(ctx, goTestCommand(h, dim))\n\t\t}\n\t\tres, _ := conformance.RunDimension(ctx, ha, dim)\n\t\treturn cellResultMsg{harness: h, dim: dim, result: res}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (m *Model) runRow(row int) tea.Cmd {\n\tcmds := make([]tea.Cmd, 0, len(m.dims))\n\tfor c := range m.dims {\n\t\tif cmd := m.runCell(row, c, false); cmd != nil {\n\t\t\tcmds = append(cmds, cmd)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn tea.Batch(cmds...)\n}\n\nfunc (m *Model) runAll() tea.Cmd {\n\tcmds := make([]tea.Cmd, 0, len(m.harnessed)*len(m.dims))\n\tfor r := range m.harnessed {\n\t\tfor c := range m.dims {\n\t\t\tif cmd := m.runCell(r, c, false); cmd != nil {\n\t\t\t\tcmds = append(cmds, cmd)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn tea.Batch(cmds...)\n}"
}

> AGENT

You were right to push back — I'd been validating a single manual paste, not the keys you actually press. This time I reproduced it against the **real `ao evalrig` TUI** and verified the fix the same way.

## The bug (reproduced)

Pressing **`a`/`A`** fires every cell's check in its own goroutine; each typed `paste`+`Enter` into the stage, and they **interleaved** → `…-count=1go test…` → `invalid value "1go"`. I confirmed it by sending `a` to the real deck pane and seeing all six commands mashed on one line.

## The fix (verified against the real TUI)

1. **Serialized stage writes** — a mutex makes each `paste`+`Enter` atomic, so even rapid presses can't interleave.
2. **Only single-cell runs touch the stage** — `enter`/`space`/`r` show one test; `a`/`A` just fill the matrix in-process (no flood, no garble).

Then I drove the actual deck headlessly and checked the real stage:
- `a` (run row) → stage stays clean, **0** garbled lines
- single `enter` → exactly **1** clean command → `--- PASS: TestConformance/claude-code/spawn … ok …conformance`
- **3 rapid enters** → still **0** garbling

Plus a `-race` regression test (`TestStageSerializesConcurrentWrites`: 16 concurrent `Run`s produce perfectly paired paste→Enter, never two pastes in a row). Full build + lint + `-race` green.

## What you'll see now

```bash
test/evalrig/demo.sh
```

- **`enter`** on a cell → one real `go test … PASS` scrolls in the stage, cell flips.
- **`a` / `A`** → the matrix fills fast (verdicts are in-process); the stage isn't touched.

### ✅ Task 1 — Wire session manager to real agent adapters  ·  `DONE (Jun 2) — incl. per-session selection`

- [x] **Per-session selection:** new `ports.AgentResolver` port; `Manager` resolves the adapter from `cfg.Harness` on Spawn and the stored harness on Restore. One daemon spawns claude **and** codex by harness; empty harness → `AO_AGENT` default; unknown harness → loud error.
- [x] Decided: left `noopMessenger` as-is — real agent nudges need the runtime/agent plugin (tracked in Backlog, not blocking).
- [x] `go build` ✅ + `go vet` ✅; touched packages pass `-race` (config, daemon, session, integration, adapters). New test `TestWiring_SessionManagerResolvesRealAgentsPerHarness` proves per-harness resolution.

### Task 2 — opencode adapter + hooks  ·  `DONE (Jun 2)`

Implements the 6-method `ports.Agent` interface. Mirrors codex for the adapter
methods, but the hook mechanism diverges (see research note below).

- [x] `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencode/opencode.go` — 6 methods
      (GetConfigSpec, GetLaunchCommand, GetPromptDeliveryStrategy, GetAgentHooks,
      GetRestoreCommand, SessionInfo) + binary resolver + manifest.
- [x] **Researched opencode's hook/config mechanism.** Key finding: opencode has
      **no native command-hook config** (no settings.local.json / hooks.json
      analogue — there's an open FR, sst/opencode#5409, asking for one). Its only
      lifecycle surface is a **JS/TS plugin** loaded from `.opencode/plugins/`
      (opencode globs `{plugin,plugins}/*.{ts,js}`). So hooks are installed by
      writing an AO-owned plugin file, not by merging JSON.
- [x] `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencode/hooks.go` + embedded
      `assets/ao-activity.ts` — installs SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/Stop,
      idempotent (atomic overwrite of AO's own file; sentinel-guarded uninstall),
      command prefix `ao hooks opencode <event>`. Event mapping (validated against
      the entire-cli reference at `~/Projects/entire-cli/.../agent/opencode`):
      `session.created`→session-start, `message.updated`/`message.part.updated`→
      user-prompt-submit, `session.status`(idle)→stop. **NB: `session.status`,
      not the deprecated `session.idle`** (unreliable in `opencode run`).
- [x] Registered opencode in the daemon agent registry
      (`daemon/lifecycle_wiring.go buildAgentRegistry`) + `opencode_test.go`
      (12 tests, mirrors codex_test.go) + extended the daemon wiring resolver test.
- [x] **Done:** `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint` all clean;

## 🚀 Run it: paste these into `/goal`

> `/goal` (Claude Code v2.1.139+, trusted workspace, hooks enabled) runs Claude autonomously turn after
> turn until a condition is met. A small evaluator model checks the condition **against what Claude
> surfaces in the transcript** — it does NOT run commands itself. Every condition below is written to be
> objectively checkable from that output.

**5 rules that make completion evaluate correctly:**

1. **Force the proof into the transcript** — say "show the full output"; the check rides on commands Claude actually runs.
2. **Objective end-states only** — "file has sections X/Y/Z", "command exits 0". Never "clean"/"good" (the evaluator can't judge taste → never converges).
3. **Anti-cheat guard** — "do not skip/delete/weaken any test", so the loop can't satisfy the evaluator by gutting the check.
4. **Bound open-ended work** — "exactly 2 adapters", not "all agents", or the loop never ends.
5. **One goal per task/day** — a week-long mega-goal isn't a single yes/no; it just burns tokens.
6. **Scope the test to what you changed** — `go test ./internal/daemon/...`, not `./...`. (Learned on Task 1: a pre-existing failure in unrelated in-progress code made `./...` red and would have sent the goal loop chasing a bug that wasn't ours.)

- **emdash parity (researched + built Jun 5):** emdash ships ~31 agents; AO now covers **22** emdash agents — **23 adapters incl. aider** (AO-only). Revisit codebuff/gemini if/when their headless stories change.
- **Lint debt (adapter fleet):** the adapters trip non-default linters `prealloc` (`cmd = []string{binary}`) and `revive` (colon-style method comments, e.g. `// GetPromptDeliveryStrategy:`). This is pre-existing house style across grok/codex/etc., not new — worth a single repo-wide cleanup pass rather than per-adapter.

Pre-existing, in the in-progress tmux runtime work — likely wants `remain-on-exit on` / a persistent shell. NOT caused by Task 1.
- HTTP routes mounting SessionManager (daemon lane)
- Full in-app browser implementation (after Task 4 design is approved)
- Full annotation implementation (after Task 6 design is approved)
- 🧹 **Decide: keep or drop `Agent.GetConfigSpec`** (revisit *after* the agent-adapter PRs are raised). Today it's dead scaffolding: **zero production callers** (only `_test.go` invokes it), **all 6 adapters return empty `ports.ConfigSpec{}`**, nothing consumes `ConfigSpec`/`ConfigField`, and the tests only assert emptiness. Intended-but-unrealized uses: (1) surfacing agent-specific config keys to users (config/doctor/OpenAPI → FE settings form), (2) validating `LaunchConfig.Config` against a declared schema before launch. Both are YAGNI until an adapter actually has custom keys. Clean deletion if we drop it (interface method + types + 6 no-op impls + emptiness tests).

6	// The Electron main process is the app's thin supervisor: it owns the window
7	// and is the ONLY layer that talks to the loopback daemon over HTTP. The
8	// renderer never reaches the network directly — it calls `window.ao.request`,
9	// which round-trips through the `ao:request` IPC channel below. This keeps the
10	// daemon loopback-only, sidesteps browser CORS, and matches the repo rule that
11	// daemon logic must not move into the UI surface.
12	
13	/** Shape returned to the renderer for every proxied daemon call. */
14	interface AoResponse {
15	  ok: boolean;
16	  status: number;
17	  data: unknown;
18	  error?: string;
19	}
20	
21	interface AoRequest {
22	  method: string;
23	  path: string;
24	  query?: Record<string, string | number | boolean | undefined>;
25	  body?: unknown;
26	}
27	
28	/**
29	 * Resolve the daemon base URL. The daemon writes its live pid/port to a
30	 * handshake file on start (AO_RUN_FILE, defaulting to the user config dir), so
31	 * we read the port from there and fall back to AO_PORT / 3001. The host is
32	 * always loopback — the daemon refuses to bind anything else.
33	 */
34	function daemonBaseURL(): string {
35	  const port = discoverPort();
36	  return `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`;
37	}
38	
39	function runFilePath(): string {
40	  if (process.env.AO_RUN_FILE) return process.env.AO_RUN_FILE;
41	  const configHome =
42	    process.env.XDG_CONFIG_HOME || join(homedir(), ".config");
43	  return join(configHome, "agent-orchestrator", "running.json");
44	}
45	
46	function discoverPort(): number {
47	  try {
48	    const raw = readFileSync(runFilePath(), "utf8");
49	    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as { port?: number };
50	    if (parsed.port) return parsed.port;
51	  } catch {
52	    // No handshake file yet (daemon not started) — fall through to env/default.
53	  }
54	  const envPort = Number(process.env.AO_PORT);
55	  return Number.isFinite(envPort) && envPort > 0 ? envPort : 3001;
56	}
57	
58	function buildURL(base: string, path: string, query?: AoRequest["query"]): string {
59	  const url = new URL(path.replace(/^\/+/, "/"), base);
60	  if (query) {
61	    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(query)) {
62	      if (value !== undefined) url.searchParams.set(key, String(value));
63	    }
64	  }
65	  return url.toString();
66	}
67	
68	async function proxyToDaemon(req: AoRequest): Promise<AoResponse> {
69	  const base = daemonBaseURL();
70	  const url = buildURL(base, req.path, req.query);
71	  try {
72	    const res = await fetch(url, {
73	      method: req.method,
74	      headers: req.body ? { "Content-Type": "application/json" } : undefined,
75	      body: req.body ? JSON.stringify(req.body) : undefined,
76	    });
77	    const text = await res.text();
78	    const data = text ? safeJSON(text) : null;
79	    return { ok: res.ok, status: res.status, data };
80	  } catch (err) {
81	    // Connection refused etc. — the daemon is almost certainly not running.
82	    return {
83	      ok: false,
84	      status: 0,
85	      data: null,
86	      error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),
87	    };
88	  }
89	}
90	
91	function safeJSON(text: string): unknown {
92	  try {
93	    return JSON.parse(text);
94	  } catch {
95	    return text;
96	  }
97	}
98

# WebContentsView Summary

**What it is:** A View component that displays web content within an Electron application, inheriting from the `View` class.

**Deprecation note:** The documentation lists `BrowserView` as deprecated, suggesting `WebContentsView` is its modern replacement.

**Attachment & positioning:** Views are added to a window's content hierarchy using `win.contentView.addChildView(view)`, then positioned with the `setBounds()` method specifying coordinates and dimensions.

**Accessing webContents:** The `view.webContents` property provides access to the underlying WebContents object, enabling operations like `view.webContents.loadURL('https://example.com')`.

**Version info:** The documentation doesn't explicitly state the introduction version, though it's presented as current API in the latest docs.

# Electron's Official Position on `<webview>`

**Not Recommended.** Electron explicitly warns against using the tag:

> "Electron's `webview` tag is based on Chromium's `webview`, which is undergoing dramatic architectural changes. This impacts the stability of `webviews`, including rendering, navigation, and event routing. We currently recommend to not use the `webview` tag and to consider alternatives."

**Recommended Alternatives:**
- `iframe`
- `WebContentsView`
- Architecture avoiding embedded content entirely

**Key Issues:**
- Runs in a separate process (unlike `iframe`)
- Architectural instability due to ongoing Chromium changes
- Known problems with rendering, navigation, and event routing
- Most methods require synchronous main process calls

The documentation makes clear this is a deprecated approach with significant stability concerns.
```

> AGENT

Confirmed against Electron's own docs. Here's the renderer-option analysis, grounded in your Electron 33 setup and the thin-supervisor architecture.

## TL;DR — use `WebContentsView`

For Electron 33, this isn't close. `BrowserView` is deprecated, `<webview>` is *officially discouraged*, `iframe` can't be a real browser — `WebContentsView` is the one supported, stable option, and it happens to align perfectly with your "main process owns everything network" rule.

## The four candidates

| Option | Status (Electron 33) | Layout model | Where the page's `webContents` lives | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`WebContentsView`** | ✅ Official, GA since v30 | Native overlay (composited at pixel bounds; not in the DOM) | **Main process** (`view.webContents`) | ✅ **Pick** |
| `<webview>` tag | ⚠️ "We recommend not to use it" — Chromium churn breaks rendering/nav/event routing; separate process; most methods need sync main calls | DOM element (flows in React layout) | Renderer (reach main via `getWebContentsId()`) | ✗ unstable |
| `BrowserView` | ⛔ Deprecated, slated for removal | Native overlay (same as WebContentsView) | Main process | ✗ deprecated |
| `iframe` | ✅ Stable | DOM element | Renderer (sandboxed) | ✗ not a browser |

`iframe` is a non-starter for a *browser*: most real sites send `X-Frame-Options`/`CSP frame-ancestors` that refuse to be framed, and you get no real navigation/driving control. Electron lists it as an "alternative," but only for cooperative embeds.

## Why `WebContentsView` is the right fit *for this app specifically*

1. **The browsed page's `webContents` lives in the main process** — which is exactly where your architecture already puts everything privileged. `main.ts` is the *only* layer that talks to the daemon ("daemon logic must not move into the UI surface"). Agent-driving the browser — `view.webContents.loadURL()`, `.executeJavaScript()`, CDP via `.debugger`, `.capturePage()` — all happens in main, reachable from the agent path **without the renderer in the loop**. So the renderer choice *pre-answers* design-doc question #3 (how agents drive/observe the browser): it's the same decision.
2. **Crash + security isolation** — the page is its own `WebContents`, sandboxed; it can't touch the React UI or your `preload` bridge.
3. **It's the only non-deprecated, non-discouraged option** — for a feature an agent must *reliably* drive, `<webview>`'s instability is disqualifying, and it wouldn't even save the main-process plumbing (you'd still bounce through `getWebContentsId()`).

## The one real cost — and how we pay it

`WebContentsView` is a **native overlay**, not a DOM node: it composites on top of the renderer at pixel coordinates, so it doesn't flow in React's layout. Three consequences, all standard patterns:

- **Bounds-sync** — put a placeholder `<div className="browser-slot">` in `sv-canvas`; a `ResizeObserver` (+ window resize + the `ResizablePanel` drag) computes its rect → IPC → `view.setBounds({x,y,width,height})`. ~30 lines.
- **z-order** — the view sits *above* renderer content, so React modals/menus can't visually overlap it. Render browser chrome (URL bar, tabs) as React *around* the slot, and hide the view (empty bounds / `removeChildView`) when a modal opens over it.
- **Lifecycle** — show/hide as `SessionView` opens/closes; one view per session vs. a shared singleton (open question below).

## Concrete wiring for this codebase

```
main.ts        ipcMain.handle("browser:create" | "navigate" | "setBounds" | "exec" | "destroy")
               → creates WebContentsView, win.contentView.addChildView(view)
preload.ts     window.ao.browser = { create, navigate, setBounds, onState, … }   (mirrors window.ao.request)
renderer       <BrowserPane> in SessionView's sv-canvas: the slot div + ResizeObserver → setBounds;
               a React URL bar / tabs above it; subscribes to nav-state events for back/forward/loading
```

It slots into the existing `sv-canvas` exactly where `<Terminal>` lives today — likely as a **tab or split** alongside the terminal (Terminal | Browser), which fits the `ResizablePanelGroup` already there.

## Open questions this surfaces (they feed the rest of the doc)

- **One `WebContentsView` per session, or one shared singleton** repositioned per active session? (memory vs. state-preservation)
- **How does the *agent* reach main's `webContents`?** Through the daemon (`ao browser …` command → daemon → ? ) or a more direct bridge? This is design-doc Q2/Q3 and is the meatiest decision — the renderer choice makes it *possible* in main, but doesn't decide the transport.
- **CDP exposure** — do we attach `webContents.debugger` (Chrome DevTools Protocol) so the agent gets the full automation surface (DOM, input, screenshots), or a narrower custom verb set?

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the VS Code Simple Browser extension implementation regarding iframe and webview architecture:

## Simple Browser Extension Overview

The Simple Browser extension uses a webview to render webpages directly in VS Code. It provides a very basic browser preview using an iframe embedded in a webview.

## Architecture and Limitations

The browser has a number of limitations due to the security around iframes, including that it traps keyboard focus, can't detect if a page fails to load, and can't track the current url of the iframe.

## Webview Architecture Details

A webview is like an iframe within VS Code that your extension controls. A webview can render almost any HTML content in this frame, and it communicates with extensions using message passing.

## Implementation Pattern

Webviews are implemented as isolated environments that communicate with the workbench via an asynchronous messaging bridge. To ensure security and performance, webviews are hosted in iframe elements (even in Electron) and utilize Service Workers for local resource loading.

The Simple Browser extension represents a practical implementation of VS Code's webview API, using nested iframes to display external web content while maintaining the security isolation that VS Code requires for webview environments.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about selecting DOM elements in preview, sending to AI coding agents, and how it integrates with dev servers:

## Key Tools and Approaches

### Stagewise
Stagewise started as a browser toolbar and is pivoting to a full "developer browser" (Electron-based). It runs `npx stagewise@latest` which starts a CLI proxy on port 3100 and injects a toolbar into your running app. It operates directly in your browser through a visual toolbar interface, allowing developers to select DOM elements and make AI-powered changes to their local codebase.

### Onlook
Onlook uses a sandboxed web container, not your real dev server. This makes it safer for experimentation but means it doesn't see your actual runtime environment — middleware, environment variables, real API responses, etc. However, you can always right-click an element to open up the exact location of the element in code.

### Frontman (Dev Server Middleware Approach)
Frontman installs as middleware inside your framework's dev server (Next.js, Astro, or Vite). Because it runs inside the framework, it has native access to both client-side context (DOM, component tree, computed styles, click targets) and server-side context (routes, compiled module graph, server logs, framework-specific state).

### Domscribe
For precise source mapping, Domscribe bridges both directions: click a DOM element to tell your agent what to change, or let your agent query any source location to see exactly what it looks like live in the browser. It walks your JSX and Vue templates, assigns each element a stable ID, and writes a manifest that maps every ID to its exact file, line, and column.
