Excellent question — and it's the one that actually *locks in* the renderer choice, because annotation = reaching into the page's DOM, and that's precisely where the iframe model dies and `WebContentsView` shines.

## How VS Code does it (and why you shouldn't copy it)

VS Code's **Simple Browser is an `<iframe>` inside a webview** — and VS Code webviews are *themselves* iframes (nested iframes for isolation), even on the desktop. ([webview API](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/webview), [simple-browser PR](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/109276), [Matt Bierner on webviews-on-web](https://blog.mattbierner.com/vscode-webview-web-learnings/)). The Simple Browser README itself lists the tells of the iframe wall: it "traps keyboard focus, can't detect if a page fails to load, and **can't track the current url of the iframe.**"

Why iframes, not Electron's native views? Because **VS Code must also run on the web** (vscode.dev / github.dev), where `BrowserView`/`WebContentsView` don't exist. So it standardized on iframe webviews for portability — and *ate* the limitations. **You're a desktop Electron app. You don't have that constraint, so you shouldn't inherit that ceiling.**

## The crux: the same-origin wall vs. privileged injection

This is the key technical point for your concern:

- An **`<iframe>`** loading a cross-origin URL is sealed by the **same-origin policy** — the parent page (your React UI) **cannot read or touch the iframe's DOM**. That's a browser security boundary, not a config you can flip. VS Code can't annotate arbitrary pages for exactly this reason.
- A **`WebContentsView`** is *not* a sibling frame — it's the embedder. Same-origin policy **does not apply** to how you reach into it. You get **two** privileged paths to the DOM **of any loaded URL**:
  1. **`webContents.executeJavaScript(...)`** — runs code *as the page* (like a DevTools console / content script). Full DOM read/write, draw overlays, capture selectors — on any origin.
  2. **`webContents.debugger`** = the **Chrome DevTools Protocol**. `DOM.getDocument` (the whole tree), `Overlay.highlightNode` (the literal inspector highlight), `DOM.getBoxModel`, `Runtime.evaluate`, input synthesis, screenshots — the same surface Playwright/Puppeteer/Chrome DevTools use.

Both run **from the main process** — which, again, is exactly where your architecture already wants privileged work.

## So: yes, your users can annotate UI elements/components — here's the honest breakdown

| What you want to annotate | Mechanism | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| **Raw DOM elements** of *any* preview URL | `executeJavaScript` or CDP `DOM`/`Overlay` | element under cursor, bounding box, CSS selector, highlight overlay |
| **Components** (e.g. "the `<Sidebar>`") of *the user's own app* | injection **+ a build-time source map** | DOM node → React component → **`file:line:col`**, so the agent edits the right source |

The second row is the rich one you're really asking about. Raw DOM you get for free; **component-level** annotation needs the page to *carry* source info — which you add with a **Vite plugin** (you already use Vite) that stamps `data-ao-source="file:line"` on each element at build time, or by reading React fiber's `_debugSource` in dev. Then "user circled this button" becomes "edit `Sidebar.tsx:42`."

This is well-trodden — every serious "see your frontend" tool works this way, none of them via a plain iframe ([overview](https://dev.to/bluehotdog/ai-coding-tools-that-actually-see-your-browser-2026-2hoc)):
- **[stagewise](https://github.com/stagewise-io/stagewise)** — injects a toolbar into your running app (CLI proxy on :3100), select element → AI edits source; now pivoting to an **Electron "developer browser"** (same conclusion you're reaching).
- **[Onlook](https://github.com/onlook-dev/onlook)** — Electron, right-click element → jump to exact source location.
- **[Frontman](https://frontman.sh/)** — dev-server middleware → native DOM + component tree + computed styles.
- **[Domscribe](https://www.domscribe.com/)** — walks JSX/Vue, assigns each element a stable ID, writes a manifest mapping ID → file:line:col (bidirectional).
- **[Chrome DevTools MCP](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-devtools-mcp)** — the CDP-for-agents path.

## What this means for the design

**The annotation requirement is the strongest argument for `WebContentsView` and against the VS Code iframe model.** It doesn't just *allow* DOM annotation — it's the only one of the four options that does, on arbitrary URLs.

Concrete shape for component annotation:
```
Vite plugin (user's app)   stamps data-ao-source="src/.../Sidebar.tsx:42:7" on elements
main.ts                    after loadURL → executeJavaScript(annotationOverlay.js) into the view
overlay (in-page)          hover/click → reads data-ao-source + selector + box → postMessage
preload/main               receives annotation → window.ao + daemon → agent context (this is Task 6 / "agentation")
CDP (fallback)             for non-instrumented URLs: DOM/Overlay/box-model gives selector+highlight, no source
```

One real **open question for Task 6**: draw the highlight **in-page** (injected overlay div — pixel-perfect, follows scroll, but lives in the page) vs. **above** (a transparent overlay synced via CDP box-models — cleaner separation, more coordinate plumbing). Most tools do in-page.

Grounded. Two facts that decide this:

1. **The desktop app *polls* the daemon today** (`App.tsx`: `setInterval(poll, POLL_MS)`; `SessionView` every 2s) — there's **no** daemon→app push channel yet.
2. But the backend already has the **CDC broadcaster** built for exactly this: `cdc/poller.go` tails `change_log`, `cdc/broadcast.go` `Subscribe(fn)` fans out, and `cdc/event.go` literally says *"Future SSE/event endpoints can subscribe here too… subscribers track their own offset (SSE Last-Event-ID)."* The push rail is half-built; no HTTP endpoint exposes it yet.

## The decision: agent↔browser transport

**Core insight:** the agent (a CLI process in a worktree) and the browser (the `WebContentsView` in the Electron app) are in **different processes that share only the daemon**. So the daemon *must* broker — and it's the right hub anyway (it already owns sessions, the CLI surface, and the event bus).

```
agent (CLI, worktree) ──HTTP──► daemon ◄──HTTP/SSE──► Electron app (owns the WebContentsView)
        ao browser …         (session "browser"        executes on webContents
        annotations           capability + broker)      (executeJS / CDP), posts results back
```

**Recommendation — a daemon-brokered session "browser" capability:**
- **Agent surface:** `ao browser <verb>` CLI → `POST /sessions/{id}/browser/…`. Universal (every adapter can shell out; mirrors `ao hooks` / `ao send`). An **MCP tool** is a thin wrapper over the same daemon API — a fast-follow for the MCP-capable agents (claude-code/codex/cursor), not the foundation.
- **Executor:** the Electron app *registers* as the session's browser executor and runs commands on the `WebContentsView`. (Treating "executor" as a capability — not hardwired to Electron — leaves room for a headless one later.)
- **Push:** build the **SSE endpoint over the existing CDC broadcaster** — it's the intended direction and the only piece of genuinely new infra.

**The natural v1 / v2 split** (this is what makes it "quick"):
- **v1 — observe** (matches your annotation concern): user annotates an element → Electron **POSTs** annotation (selector + `data-ao-source` + screenshot) to the daemon → it lands as agent context. This is **Electron→daemon only — no push channel needed**, so it ships fast and delivers the actual goal (user annotates UI → agent acts).
- **v2 — drive** (agent → browser): needs the daemon→Electron **SSE** push. Build it second.

# Agentation: Visual Feedback Tool for AI Agents

## (1) Selection Mechanism
Agentation is a **React 18+ library** installed via npm. Users import and add the `<Agentation />` component to their app. The toolbar appears in the bottom-right corner, and users activate it to click elements for annotation. It supports click selection, text selection, multi-select via dragging, and area selection.

## (2) Element Reference Capture
The tool captures **CSS selectors and element positions**. According to the docs: "Agentation captures class names, selectors, and element positions so AI agents can `grep` for the exact code you're referring to."

## (3) Annotation Data Model
The repo doesn't expose the internal data structure in this content, but it produces **structured markdown output** that includes selectors, positions, and context about annotated elements.

## (4) Data Delivery to AI Agents
Users **copy structured output to clipboard**. The description states: "Copy markdown with selectors, positions, and context." This clipboard data can then be pasted into prompts for AI coding agents.

## (5) Tech Stack & Key Directories
- **Languages**: TypeScript (84.1%), SCSS (9.0%), HTML/CSS (3.3% each)
- **Key directories**: `/package` (npm package), `/mcp` (likely Model Context Protocol integration), `/skills`
- **Build files**: `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `vercel.json` (deployment)
- **License**: PolyForm Shield 1.0.0

# Agentation MCP Overview

## Files in the Directory
The `mcp` directory contains:
- `src/` (source code folder)
- `.gitignore`
- `README.md`
- `package.json`
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`
- `tsconfig.json`
- `tsup.config.ts`

## Server Function
The MCP server provides visual feedback integration for AI coding agents by managing annotations created through a browser toolbar.

## MCP Tools Exposed
The server exposes eight tools:
- `agentation_list_sessions`
- `agentation_get_session`
- `agentation_get_pending`
- `agentation_get_all_pending`
- `agentation_acknowledge`
- `agentation_resolve`
- `agentation_dismiss`
- `agentation_reply`
- `agentation_watch_annotations`

## Annotation Reception Method
Annotations arrive via an **HTTP server** (default port 4747). The server accepts POST requests to create annotations and provides a Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream at `GET /sessions/:id/events` for real-time updates.

## Agent Connection
Agents connect through the MCP protocol using stdio. Installation is simplified with:
```
claude mcp add agentation -- npx agentation-mcp server
```
The server simultaneously runs the HTTP endpoint and exposes the MCP tools for Claude Code integration.
```

> AGENT

This is the unlock. agentation is essentially a **mini-daemon**, and its architecture maps almost 1:1 onto what you already have:

| agentation | your daemon today |
|---|---|
| HTTP server (:4747), **POST** to ingest annotations | loopback HTTP daemon + session routes |
| **SSE** `GET /sessions/:id/events` | CDC broadcaster (`cdc/broadcast.go`), built *for* SSE |
| session model + **pending** annotations | session model (`change_log`, triggers) |
| 8 MCP tools: `agentation_get_pending` / `_acknowledge` / `_resolve` / `_reply` / `_watch_annotations` | — (this is the surface to mirror) |
| `<Agentation/>` React component captures selector+classNames+position → markdown | — (the capture overlay) |

So the agent-surface question answers itself: **don't run agentation's parallel server — mirror its model into our daemon.** It even validates "observe-first": its whole loop is *agent pulls `get_pending` annotations + `watch`*, exactly your v1.

## The decision (agent ↔ browser surface, agentation-informed)

- **Annotations live on our session, ingested over our daemon** — `POST /sessions/{id}/annotations` (agentation's POST), persisted like everything else. One session model, not two.
- **Agent reads via `ao` CLI** — verbs cloned from agentation's tools: `ao annotations pending|resolve|reply` (+ `watch` once SSE lands). Universal across the whole adapter fleet. An **MCP wrapper** is the fast-follow for claude/codex (agentation proves that design works).
- **Capture overlay** = agentation's `<Agentation/>` component pointed at our endpoint, *or* our own injected overlay — and it uses **grep-able selectors + classNames** (no Vite source-map plugin needed), which simplifies what I'd proposed earlier.

⚠️ **One flag:** agentation is **PolyForm Shield 1.0.0** (source-available, *no-compete*). Mirroring the *design/API* is fine; **vendoring their code** into an agent-orchestrator product is a license risk worth checking before we reuse `<Agentation/>` or `agentation-mcp` directly.

## Locked decisions
1. **Renderer** → `WebContentsView` (Electron 33; the only supported + DOM-accessible option)
2. **DOM access** → privileged injection (`executeJavaScript`) + CDP, on any URL — the thing iframes/VS Code can't do
3. **Transport** → daemon-brokered, modelled on agentation: `POST /sessions/{id}/annotations`, read via `ao annotations …` (MCP wrapper later)
4. **Scope** → **v1 = observe-first** (user annotates → agent context); agent-driving is v2

## v1 build order (now unambiguous)
1. **Spike** — `WebContentsView` in `SessionView`'s `sv-canvas` + URL bar + `loadURL` + bounds-sync
2. **Capture → ingest** — injected overlay: click → selector/classNames/box → `POST …/annotations`
3. **Daemon annotation capability** — route + persistence + `ao annotations pending|resolve|reply`
4. **SSE** over the CDC broadcaster (enables `watch`, unblocks v2)

## COMPREHENSIVE IMPLEMENTATION REPORT: In-App Browser Annotation Feature Path

Based on thorough code exploration, here's the complete architecture and exact patterns for implementing the annotation feature:

---

### 1. SESSION HTTP ROUTES & REQUEST/RESPONSE DTYPES

**File: `/backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go`**

**Route Registration (Register function):**
Lines 55-68 show the pattern:
```go
func (c *SessionsController) Register(r chi.Router) {
	r.Get("/sessions", c.list)
	r.Post("/sessions", c.spawn)
	r.Post("/sessions/cleanup", c.cleanup)
	r.Get("/sessions/{sessionId}", c.get)
	r.Patch("/sessions/{sessionId}", c.rename)
	r.Post("/sessions/{sessionId}/restore", c.restore)
	r.Post("/sessions/{sessionId}/kill", c.kill)
	r.Post("/sessions/{sessionId}/send", c.send)      // <-- existing send handler
	r.Post("/sessions/{sessionId}/activity", c.activity)
	// ... orchestrator routes
}
```

**Existing `POST /sessions/{id}/send` Handler (c.send):**
Lines 191-215:
```go
func (c *SessionsController) send(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if c.Svc == nil {
		apispec.NotImplemented(w, r, "POST", "/api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/send")
		return
	}
	var in SendSessionMessageRequest
	if err := decodeJSON(r, &in); err != nil {
		envelope.WriteAPIError(w, r, http.StatusBadRequest, "bad_request", "INVALID_JSON", "Invalid JSON body", nil)
		return
	}
	if in.Message == "" {
		envelope.WriteAPIError(w, r, http.StatusBadRequest, "bad_request", "MESSAGE_REQUIRED", "Message is required", nil)
		return
	}
	if len(in.Message) > maxMessageLen {
		envelope.WriteAPIError(w, r, http.StatusBadRequest, "bad_request", "MESSAGE_TOO_LONG", "Message is too long", nil)
		return
	}
	message := stripUnsafeControlChars(in.Message)
	if err := c.Svc.Send(r.Context(), sessionID(r), message); err != nil {
		envelope.WriteError(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	envelope.WriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, SendSessionMessageResponse{OK: true, SessionID: sessionID(r), Message: message})
}
```

**Request/Response DTOs:**
File: `/backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go`, lines 166-176:

```go
// SendSessionMessageRequest is the body of POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/send.
type SendSessionMessageRequest struct {
	Message string `json:"message" minLength:"1" maxLength:"4096"`
}

// SendSessionMessageResponse is the body of POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/send.
type SendSessionMessageResponse struct {
	OK        bool             `json:"ok"`
	SessionID domain.SessionID `json:"sessionId"`
	Message   string           `json:"message"`
}
```

**Pattern for New Annotation Route:**
- Add to Register: `r.Post("/sessions/{sessionId}/annotations", c.annotations)`
- Create similar handler that validates annotation payload and calls `c.Svc.Send()` with formatted annotation message
- Define DTOs `PostAnnotationRequest` and `PostAnnotationResponse` in dto.go

### 2. SEND-MESSAGE PATH END-TO-END

**Trace: Controller → Service → Messenger → Runtime → Zellij**

**Step 1: Controller c.send (lines 191-215, sessions.go)**
- Validates message, strips unsafe control chars
- Calls: `c.Svc.Send(r.Context(), sessionID(r), message)`
- `c.Svc` is type `SessionService` (interface defined lines 26-36)

**Step 2: Session Service Send (lines 100-103, backend/internal/service/session/service.go)**
```go
// Send delegates agent messaging to the internal manager.
func (s *Service) Send(ctx context.Context, id domain.SessionID, message string) error {
	return toAPIError(s.manager.Send(ctx, id, message))
}
```
- `s.manager` is `*sessionmanager.Manager`

**Step 3: Session Manager Send (lines 268-274, backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go)**
```go
// Send delivers a message to a running session's agent via the messenger.
func (m *Manager) Send(ctx context.Context, id domain.SessionID, message string) error {
	if err := m.messenger.Send(ctx, id, message); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("send %s: %w", id, err)
	}
	return nil
}
```
- `m.messenger` is type `ports.AgentMessenger` (interface lines 18-21, backend/internal/ports/outbound.go):
```go
type AgentMessenger interface {
	Send(ctx context.Context, id domain.SessionID, message string) error
}
```

**Step 4: Runtime Messenger Send (lines 91-107, backend/internal/daemon/lifecycle_wiring.go)**
```go
type runtimeMessenger struct {
	store   *sqlite.Store
	runtime runtimeMessageSender
}

func (m runtimeMessenger) Send(ctx context.Context, id domain.SessionID, message string) error {
	rec, ok, err := m.store.GetSession(ctx, id)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !ok {
		return fmt.Errorf("session %s: %w", id, sessionmanager.ErrNotFound)
	}
	if rec.IsTerminated {
		return fmt.Errorf("session %s: %w", id, sessionmanager.ErrTerminated)
	}
	handleID := rec.Metadata.RuntimeHandleID
	if handleID == "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("session %s: %w", id, sessionmanager.ErrIncompleteHandle)
	}
	return m.runtime.SendMessage(ctx, ports.RuntimeHandle{ID: handleID}, message)
}
```
- `m.runtime` is type `runtimeMessageSender` (interface lines 79-81):
```go
type runtimeMessageSender interface {
	SendMessage(ctx context.Context, handle ports.RuntimeHandle, message string) error
}
```

**Step 5: Zellij Runtime SendMessage (lines 174-188, backend/internal/adapters/runtime/zellij/zellij.go)**
```go
// SendMessage pastes a message into the session's pane (chunked) and presses
// Enter to submit it.
func (r *Runtime) SendMessage(ctx context.Context, handle ports.RuntimeHandle, message string) error {
	id, paneID, err := handleID(handle)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for _, chunk := range chunks(message, r.chunkSize) {
		if _, err := r.run(ctx, pasteArgs(id, paneID, chunk)...); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("zellij runtime: paste message %s/%s: %w", id, paneID, err)
		}
	}
	if _, err := r.run(ctx, sendEnterArgs(id, paneID)...); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("zellij runtime: send enter %s/%s: %w", id, paneID, err)
	}
	return nil
}
```
- **Key: This chunks the message, pastes it to the zellij pane via `zellij input text` commands, then sends Enter**
- The chunks use `r.chunkSize` to respect zellij paste limits
- The `run()` calls execute `zellij input` subcommands via the zellij CLI

**Critical Implementation Point:**
To deliver an annotation, you format it as a message string (e.g., `[ANNOTATION] {content}`) and pass it through this exact same Send chain. The annotation reaches the agent's terminal as if the user had typed it.

---

### 3. TERMINAL WEBSOCKET / MUX

**WebSocket Server Setup:**

**File: `/backend/internal/httpd/terminal_mux.go`**

Lines 20-46 show the implementation:

```go
// mountTerminalMux registers the long-lived terminal-multiplexing WebSocket at /mux. It
// is intentionally outside the per-request Timeout middleware (the connection is
// long-lived). When mgr is nil the route is not mounted — the daemon simply has
// no terminal surface yet.
func mountTerminalMux(r chi.Router, mgr *terminal.Manager, log *slog.Logger) {
	if mgr == nil {
		return
	}
	r.Get("/mux", terminalMuxHandler(mgr, log))
}

// terminalMuxHandler upgrades the request to a WebSocket and hands the connection to the
// terminal manager. httpd owns only the upgrade and the transport adaptation;
// all stream logic lives in internal/terminal.
func terminalMuxHandler(mgr *terminal.Manager, log *slog.Logger) http.HandlerFunc {
	return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		// InsecureSkipVerify disables coder/websocket's same-origin check: the
		// daemon binds loopback only and the desktop renderer's origin differs
		// from the loopback host, mirroring the legacy Node mux server.
		c, err := websocket.Accept(w, r, &websocket.AcceptOptions{InsecureSkipVerify: true})
		if err != nil {
			log.Warn("terminal mux: websocket upgrade failed", "err", err)
			return
		}
		c.SetReadLimit(terminalMuxReadLimit)
		mgr.Serve(r.Context(), &terminalMuxConn{c: c})
	}
}
```

**Connection Details:**
- **Path:** `/mux` (mounted in router at line 56, backend/internal/httpd/router.go)
- **Protocol:** WebSocket, JSON text frames (via `coder/websocket` + `wsjson`)
- **Host:** `127.0.0.1:<daemon-port>` (loopback only, daemon refuses any other bind)
- **Port:** Discovered from `running.json` handshake file (see frontend/src/main.ts lines 34-56)

**Wire Protocol:**

File: `/backend/internal/terminal/protocol.go`, lines 1-71:

Client → Server frame:
```go
type clientMsg struct {
	Ch   string `json:"ch"`
	ID   string `json:"id,omitempty"`
	Type string `json:"type"`
	// Data is base64-encoded keystrokes for ch "terminal" / type "data".
	Data string `json:"data,omitempty"`
	Cols uint16 `json:"cols,omitempty"`
	Rows uint16 `json:"rows,omitempty"`
}
```

Server → Client frame:
```go
type serverMsg struct {
	Ch   string `json:"ch"`
	ID   string `json:"id,omitempty"`
	Type string `json:"type"`
	// Data is base64-encoded PTY output for ch "terminal" / type "data".
	Data    string         `json:"data,omitempty"`
	Error   string         `json:"error,omitempty"`
	Session *sessionUpdate `json:"session,omitempty"`
}
```

**Channels:**
- `"terminal"` — per-pane byte stream, keyed by runtime handle id (the pane's session handle)
- `"subscribe"` — opt into session-state changes
- `"sessions"` — server-pushed CDC session updates
- `"system"` — liveness (ping/pong)

**Terminal-Specific Messages:**
- Client: `{type: "open", id: "<handle-id>"}` — request attach to pane
- Client: `{type: "data", id: "<id>", data: "<base64-encoded-keystrokes>"}` — send input
- Client: `{type: "resize", id: "<id>", cols: N, rows: M}` — resize pane
- Client: `{type: "close", id: "<id>"}` — detach
- Server: `{type: "opened", id: "<id>"}` — attach acknowledged
- Server: `{type: "data", id: "<id>", data: "<base64-output>"}` — PTY output
- Server: `{type: "exited", id: "<id>"}` — pane exited

**Frontend Terminal Component Status:**

File: `/frontend/src/renderer/components/Terminal.tsx`, lines 4-27:

**YES, it is currently a SCAFFOLD/STUB.** The component exists but is intentionally unimplemented. Comments (lines 4-27) explain what the implementer must do:

### 4. FRONTEND DAEMON BRIDGE: IPC PROXY PATTERN

**File: `/frontend/src/main.ts`** (Electron main process)

Lines 68-89 define the daemon proxy:

```typescript
async function proxyToDaemon(req: AoRequest): Promise<AoResponse> {
  const base = daemonBaseURL();
  const url = buildURL(base, req.path, req.query);
  try {
    const res = await fetch(url, {
      method: req.method,
      headers: req.body ? { "Content-Type": "application/json" } : undefined,
      body: req.body ? JSON.stringify(req.body) : undefined,
    });
    const text = await res.text();
    const data = text ? safeJSON(text) : null;
    return { ok: res.ok, status: res.status, data };
  } catch (err) {
    // Connection refused etc. — the daemon is almost certainly not running.
    return {
      ok: false,
      status: 0,
      data: null,
      error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),
    };
  }
}
```

191	func (c *SessionsController) send(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
192		if c.Svc == nil {
193			apispec.NotImplemented(w, r, "POST", "/api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/send")
194			return
195		}
196		var in SendSessionMessageRequest
197		if err := decodeJSON(r, &in); err != nil {
198			envelope.WriteAPIError(w, r, http.StatusBadRequest, "bad_request", "INVALID_JSON", "Invalid JSON body", nil)
199			return
200		}
201		if in.Message == "" {
202			envelope.WriteAPIError(w, r, http.StatusBadRequest, "bad_request", "MESSAGE_REQUIRED", "Message is required", nil)
203			return
204		}
205		if len(in.Message) > maxMessageLen {
206			envelope.WriteAPIError(w, r, http.StatusBadRequest, "bad_request", "MESSAGE_TOO_LONG", "Message is too long", nil)
207			return
208		}
209		message := stripUnsafeControlChars(in.Message)
210		if err := c.Svc.Send(r.Context(), sessionID(r), message); err != nil {
211			envelope.WriteError(w, r, err)
212			return
213		}
214		envelope.WriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, SendSessionMessageResponse{OK: true, SessionID: sessionID(r), Message: message})
215	}

217	// activity records an agent activity-state signal reported by an agent hook
218	// (via `ao hooks <agent> <event>`). It funnels through the single
219	// lifecycle.Manager so the reaper and hooks never race on the session's
220	// activity/termination columns.
221	func (c *SessionsController) activity(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
222		if c.Activity == nil {
223			apispec.NotImplemented(w, r, "POST", "/api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/activity")
224			return
225		}
226		var in SetActivityRequest
227		if err := decodeJSON(r, &in); err != nil {
228			envelope.WriteAPIError(w, r, http.StatusBadRequest, "bad_request", "INVALID_JSON", "Invalid JSON body", nil)
229			return
230		}
231		state := domain.ActivityState(in.State)
232		switch state {
233		case domain.ActivityActive, domain.ActivityIdle, domain.ActivityWaitingInput, domain.ActivityExited:
234		default:
235			envelope.WriteAPIError(w, r, http.StatusBadRequest, "bad_request", "INVALID_ACTIVITY_STATE", "Unknown activity state", nil)
236			return
237		}
238		if err := c.Activity.ApplyActivitySignal(r.Context(), sessionID(r), ports.ActivitySignal{Valid: true, State: state}); err != nil {
239			envelope.WriteError(w, r, err)
240			return
241		}
242		envelope.WriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, SetActivityResponse{OK: true, SessionID: sessionID(r), State: in.State})
243	}

// Package specgen builds the code-first OpenAPI document from the Go contract
// types. It lives outside apispec because it imports the controllers (to
// reflect their request/response shapes), and controllers import apispec (for
// the 501 stub) — keeping Build here breaks that cycle. apispec only embeds and
// serves the committed openapi.yaml; specgen produces it.
package specgen

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"reflect"
	"strings"

	jsonschema "github.com/swaggest/jsonschema-go"
	openapi "github.com/swaggest/openapi-go"

	"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/httpd/envelope"
	projectsvc "github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/service/project"
)

// Build reflects the Go contract types and the operation registry below into
// the OpenAPI document. It is the single source of truth for the /api/v1
// contract: `cmd/genspec` writes its output to apispec/openapi.yaml (the
// committed, embedded artifact) and TestBuild_MatchesEmbedded asserts the embed
// equals fresh Build() output so the two can never drift. Schema facets live as
// struct tags on the service.*/controllers.* types; operation metadata (path,
// status codes, summaries) lives here.
//

18	// TestRouteSpecParity asserts the mounted /api/v1 routes and the OpenAPI
19	// operations are in 1:1 correspondence — so a route can't be added without
20	// spec coverage, and the spec can't describe a route that isn't served.
21	func TestRouteSpecParity(t *testing.T) {
22		log := slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(io.Discard, nil))
23		router := httpd.NewRouterWithControl(config.Config{}, log, nil, httpd.APIDeps{}, httpd.ControlDeps{})
24	
25		mounted := map[string]bool{}
26		err := chi.Walk(router, func(method, route string, _ http.Handler, _ ...func(http.Handler) http.Handler) error {
27			if strings.HasPrefix(route, "/api/v1/") && route != "/api/v1/openapi.yaml" {
28				mounted[strings.ToUpper(method)+" "+route] = true
29			}
30			return nil
31		})
32		if err != nil {
33			t.Fatalf("walk routes: %v", err)
34		}
35		if len(mounted) == 0 {
36			t.Fatal("no /api/v1 routes mounted — router wiring changed?")
37		}
38	
39		// Forward: every mounted route resolves to an operation slice.
40		for r := range mounted {
41			mp := strings.SplitN(r, " ", 2)
42			if apispec.Default().Operation(mp[0], mp[1]) == nil {
43				t.Errorf("mounted route %s has no OpenAPI operation", r)
44			}
45		}
46	
47		// Reverse: every spec operation is a mounted route.
48		var doc struct {
49			Paths map[string]map[string]yaml.Node `yaml:"paths"`
50		}
51		if err := yaml.Unmarshal(apispec.Default().YAML(), &doc); err != nil {
52			t.Fatalf("parse spec: %v", err)
53		}
54		httpMethods := map[string]bool{"get": true, "post": true, "put": true, "patch": true, "delete": true}
55		for path, item := range doc.Paths {
56			for method := range item {
57				if !httpMethods[method] {
58					continue // skip parameters, summary, etc.
59				}
60				key := strings.ToUpper(method) + " " + path
61				if !mounted[key] {
62					t.Errorf("spec operation %s has no mounted route", key)
63				}
64			}
65		}
66	}

156	// markRequestBodyRequired sets requestBody.required: true on the operation's
157	// JSON body. swaggest leaves it absent (== optional) for AddReqStructure bodies.
158	func markRequestBodyRequired(cor openapi.ContentOrReference) {
159		if rb, ok := cor.(*openapi31.RequestBodyOrReference); ok && rb.RequestBody != nil {
160			rb.RequestBody.WithRequired(true)
161		}
162	}
163	
164	// nonNullableSlices drops the "null" that swaggest unions into every Go slice
165	// type (a nil slice marshals as JSON null). A required array field should be
166	// `T[]`, not `T[] | null`; the handlers normalise nil to an empty slice, so
167	// null never reaches the wire. Byte slices (base64 strings) are left alone.

It reuses the send path: the\n// annotation is formatted into an agent-readable instruction and pasted into the\n// session's pane, exactly as `ao send` would deliver a typed message.\nfunc (c *SessionsController) annotations(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {\n\tif c.Svc == nil {\n\t\tapispec.NotImplemented(w, r, \"POST\", \"/api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/annotations\")\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tvar in AnnotationRequest\n\tif err := decodeJSON(r, &in); err != nil {\n\t\tenvelope.WriteAPIError(w, r, http.StatusBadRequest, \"bad_request\", \"INVALID_JSON\", \"Invalid JSON body\", nil)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif strings.TrimSpace(in.Selector) == \"\" {\n\t\tenvelope.WriteAPIError(w, r, http.StatusBadRequest, \"bad_request\", \"SELECTOR_REQUIRED\", \"selector is required\", nil)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tmessage := stripUnsafeControlChars(formatAnnotation(in))\n\tif len(message) > maxMessageLen {\n\t\tmessage = message[:maxMessageLen]\n\t}\n\tif err := c.Svc.Send(r.Context(), sessionID(r), message); err != nil {\n\t\tenvelope.WriteError(w, r, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tenvelope.WriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, AnnotationResponse{OK: true, SessionID: sessionID(r), Delivered: message})\n}\n\n// formatAnnotation renders a captured UI annotation into a concise instruction\n// for the agent. It leads with the grep-able selector/classes so the agent can\n// locate the element in source, and ends with the user's request.\nfunc formatAnnotation(a AnnotationRequest) string {\n\tvar b strings.Builder\n\tb.WriteString(\"[ui-annotation] The user pointed at an element in the live preview\")\n\tif u := strings.TrimSpace(a.URL); u != \"\" {\n\t\tb.WriteString(\" (\")\n\t\tb.WriteString(u)\n\t\tb.WriteString(\")\")\n\t}\n\tb.WriteString(\":\\n\")\n\tif e := strings.TrimSpace(a.Element); e != \"\" {\n\t\tb.WriteString(\"  element:  \")\n\t\tb.WriteString(e)\n\t\tb.WriteString(\"\\n\")\n\t}\n\tb.WriteString(\"  selector: \")\n\tb.WriteString(strings.TrimSpace(a.Selector))\n\tb.WriteString(\"\\n\")\n\tif t := strings.TrimSpace(a.Text); t != \"\" {\n\t\tb.WriteString(\"  text:     \\\"\")\n\t\tb.WriteString(clampRunes(t, 200))\n\t\tb.WriteString(\"\\\"\\n\")\n\t}\n\tif s := strings.TrimSpace(a.Source); s != \"\" {\n\t\tb.WriteString(\"  source:   \")\n\t\tb.WriteString(s)\n\t\tb.WriteString(\"\\n\")\n\t}\n\tif note := strings.TrimSpace(a.Note); note != \"\" {\n\t\tb.WriteString(\"  request:  \")\n\t\tb.WriteString(note)\n\t\tb.WriteString(\"\\n\")\n\t}\n\tb.WriteString(\"Locate this element in the code (grep the selector/classes) and address the request above.\")\n\treturn b.String()\n}\n\nfunc clampRunes(s string, maxRunes int) string {\n\tr := []rune(s)\n\tif len(r) <= maxRunes {\n\t\treturn s\n\t}\n\treturn string(r[:maxRunes]) + \"…\"\n}"

1	import { contextBridge, ipcRenderer } from "electron";
2	
3	// The preload is the ONLY bridge between the sandboxed renderer and the main
4	// process. It exposes a single typed `request` that forwards to the `ao:request`
5	// IPC channel (which proxies to the loopback daemon). The renderer therefore
6	// never sees `ipcRenderer` or the network directly — it just awaits `window.ao`.
7	
8	export interface AoRequest {
9	  method: string;
10	  path: string;
11	  query?: Record<string, string | number | boolean | undefined>;
12	  body?: unknown;
13	}
14	
15	export interface AoResponse<T = unknown> {
16	  ok: boolean;
17	  status: number;
18	  data: T;
19	  error?: string;
20	}
21	
22	const api = {
23	  request: <T = unknown>(req: AoRequest): Promise<AoResponse<T>> =>
24	    ipcRenderer.invoke("ao:request", req),
25	};
26	
27	contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld("ao", api);
28	
29	export type AoBridge = typeof api;

Mirrors controllers.AnnotationRequest (+ rect, which\n// the daemon ignores).\nexport interface BrowserAnnotation {\n  selector: string;\n  element?: string;\n  text?: string;\n  url?: string;\n  source?: string;\n  note?: string;\n  rect?: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number };\n}\n\ndeclare global {\n  interface Window {\n    ao: {\n      request<T = unknown>(req: {\n        method: string;\n        path: string;\n        query?: Record<string, string | number | boolean | undefined>;\n        body?: unknown;\n      }): Promise<AoResponse<T>>;\n      browser: {\n        control(msg: BrowserControlMsg): Promise<void>;\n        onState(cb: (s: BrowserState) => void): () => void;\n        onAnnotation(cb: (data: BrowserAnnotation) => void): () => void;\n      };\n    };\n  }\n}\n\n// postAnnotation delivers a captured UI annotation to the session's agent.\nexport async function postAnnotation(\n  id: string,\n  annotation: BrowserAnnotation,\n): Promise<string> {\n  const data = await unwrap(\n    window.ao.request<{ delivered: string }>({\n      method: \"POST\",\n      path: `/api/v1/sessions/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/annotations`,\n      body: annotation,\n    }),\n  );\n  return data.delivered;\n}"

{

  "content": "import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from \"react\";\nimport { postAnnotation, type BrowserAnnotation, type BrowserState } from \"../lib/api\";\n\n// BrowserPane is the in-app browser surface. The actual page renders in a native\n// WebContentsView owned by the Electron main process (see src/main.ts); this\n// React component owns the chrome (URL bar, nav, annotate toggle) and keeps the\n// view positioned over the `browser-slot` div via setBounds. The injected\n// overlay captures element annotations, which arrive here and are POSTed to the\n// session's agent. See docs/design/in-app-browser.md.\nexport function BrowserPane(props: {\n  sessionId: string;\n  onError: (msg: string) => void;\n}) {\n  const slotRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);\n  const [urlInput, setUrlInput] = useState(\"http://localhost:5173\");\n  const [state, setState] = useState<BrowserState | null>(null);\n  const [annotate, setAnnotate] = useState(false);\n  const [toast, setToast] = useState<string | null>(null);\n\n  const syncBounds = useCallback(() => {\n    const el = slotRef.current;\n    if (!el) return;\n    const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();\n    void window.ao.browser.control({\n      type: \"setBounds\",\n      bounds: {\n        x: Math.round(r.left),\n        y: Math.round(r.top),\n        width: Math.round(r.width),\n        height: Math.round(r.height),\n      },\n    });\n  }, []);\n\n  // Mount: position the view + subscribe to nav-state and annotation events.\n  // Unmount (e.g. switching tabs): hide the native view.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    syncBounds();\n    const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => syncBounds());\n    if (slotRef.current) ro.observe(slotRef.current);\n    window.addEventListener(\"resize\", syncBounds);\n\n    const offState = window.ao.browser.onState((s) => setState(s));\n    const offAnnotation = window.ao.browser.onAnnotation((data: BrowserAnnotation) => {\n      void postAnnotation(props.sessionId, data)\n        .then(() =>\n          setToast(`Sent “${data.note || data.element || data.selector}” to the agent`),\n        )\n        .catch((err) => props.onError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)));\n    });\n\n    return () => {\n      ro.disconnect();\n      window.removeEventListener(\"resize\", syncBounds);\n      offState();\n      offAnnotation();\n      void window.ao.browser.control({ type: \"hide\" });\n    };\n  }, [syncBounds, props]);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!toast) return;\n    const t = window.setTimeout(() => setToast(null), 3000);\n    return () => window.clearTimeout(t);\n  }, [toast]);\n\n  const go = () => {\n    const u = urlInput.trim();\n    if (u) void window.ao.browser.control({ type: \"navigate\", url: u });\n  };\n  const toggleAnnotate = () => {\n    const next = !annotate;\n    setAnnotate(next);\n    void window.ao.browser.control({ type: \"setAnnotateMode\", on: next });\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"browser-pane\">\n      <div className=\"browser-bar\">\n        <button\n          className=\"icon-btn\"\n          onClick={() => void window.ao.browser.control({ type: \"back\" })}\n          disabled={!state?.canGoBack}\n          title=\"Back\"\n        >\n          ‹\n        </button>\n        <button\n          className=\"icon-btn\"\n          onClick={() => void window.ao.browser.control({ type: \"forward\" })}\n          disabled={!state?.canGoForward}\n          title=\"Forward\"\n        >\n          ›\n        </button>\n        <button\n          className=\"icon-btn\"\n          onClick={() => void window.ao.browser.control({ type: \"reload\" })}\n          title=\"Reload\"\n        >\n          ⟳\n        </button>\n        <input\n          className=\"browser-url\"\n          value={urlInput}\n          onChange={(e) => setUrlInput(e.target.value)}\n          onKeyDown={(e) => e.key === \"Enter\" && go()}\n          placeholder=\"http://localhost:5173\"\n          spellCheck={false}\n        />\n        <button className=\"btn-primary sm\" onClick={go}>\n          Go\n        </button>\n        <button\n          className={annotate ? \"btn-primary sm\" : \"btn-ghost sm\"}\n          onClick={toggleAnnotate}\n          title=\"Toggle annotate mode, then click any element in the preview\"\n        >\n          {annotate ? \"● Annotating\" : \"Annotate\"}\n        </button>\n      </div>\n      <div className=\"browser-slot\" ref={slotRef}>\n        {!state?.url && (\n          <div className=\"browser-hint\">\n            Enter a preview URL (your dev server) and press <b>Go</b>. Then toggle{\" \"}\n            <b>Annotate</b> and click any element to send it to the agent.\n          </div>\n        )}\n      </div>\n      {toast && <div className=\"browser-toast\">{toast}</div>}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"
}

  "new_string": "// --- ao:mux — WebSocket terminal mux relay -----------------------------------\n//\n// The renderer is sandboxed and cannot open sockets, so the single mux\n// WebSocket to ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/mux lives here in main and frames are\n// relayed to the renderer over IPC (mirrors the ao:request bridge). Protocol:\n// backend/internal/terminal/protocol.go.\n\ninterface MuxClientFrame {\n  ch: \"terminal\" | \"system\";\n  id?: string;\n  type: \"open\" | \"data\" | \"resize\" | \"close\" | \"ping\";\n  data?: string;\n  cols?: number;\n  rows?: number;\n}\n\ninterface MuxServerFrame {\n  ch?: string;\n  id?: string;\n  type?: string;\n  data?: string;\n  error?: string;\n}\n\ninterface MuxConn {\n  ws: WebSocket | null;\n  ready: boolean;\n  pending: MuxClientFrame[];\n  open: Set<string>;\n}\n\nconst muxConns = new Map<number, MuxConn>();\n\nfunction muxURL(): string {\n  return `ws://127.0.0.1:${discoverPort()}/mux`;\n}\n\nfunction getMuxConn(wc: WebContents): MuxConn {\n  const existing = muxConns.get(wc.id);\n  if (existing) return existing;\n  const conn: MuxConn = { ws: null, ready: false, pending: [], open: new Set() };\n  muxConns.set(wc.id, conn);\n\n  const ws = new WebSocket(muxURL());\n  conn.ws = ws;\n  ws.on(\"open\", () => {\n    conn.ready = true;\n    for (const frame of conn.pending) ws.send(JSON.stringify(frame));\n    conn.pending = [];\n  });\n  ws.on(\"message\", (raw: WebSocket.RawData) => {\n    if (wc.isDestroyed()) return;\n    let frame: MuxServerFrame;\n    try {\n      frame = JSON.parse(raw.toString()) as MuxServerFrame;\n    } catch {\n      return;\n    }\n    if (frame.ch !== \"terminal\" || !frame.id) return;\n    wc.send(`ao:mux:msg:${frame.id}`, frame);\n  });\n  const teardown = (): void => {\n    conn.ready = false;\n    conn.ws = null;\n    muxConns.delete(wc.id);\n  };\n  ws.on(\"close\", teardown);\n  ws.on(\"error\", teardown);\n  return conn;\n}\n\nfunction muxSend(wc: WebContents, frame: MuxClientFrame): void {\n  const conn = getMuxConn(wc);\n  if (conn.ready && conn.ws && conn.ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {\n    conn.ws.send(JSON.stringify(frame));\n  } else {\n    conn.pending.push(frame);\n  }\n}\n\nfunction registerMuxIpc(): void {\n  ipcMain.handle(\"ao:mux:open\", (event, handleId: string) => {\n    getMuxConn(event.sender).open.add(handleId);\n    muxSend(event.sender, { ch: \"terminal\", id: handleId, type: \"open\" });\n  });\n  ipcMain.handle(\"ao:mux:send\", (event, handleId: string, data: string) => {\n    muxSend(event.sender, { ch: \"terminal\", id: handleId, type: \"data\", data });\n  });\n  ipcMain.handle(\n    \"ao:mux:resize\",\n    (event, handleId: string, cols: number, rows: number) => {\n      muxSend(event.sender, { ch: \"terminal\", id: handleId, type: \"resize\", cols, rows });\n    },\n  );\n  ipcMain.handle(\"ao:mux:close\", (event, handleId: string) => {\n    const conn = muxConns.get(event.sender.id);\n    if (conn) conn.open.delete(handleId);\n    muxSend(event.sender, { ch: \"terminal\", id: handleId, type: \"close\" });\n  });\n}\n\napp.whenReady().then(() => {\n  ipcMain.handle(\"ao:request\", (_event, req: AoRequest) => proxyToDaemon(req));\n  ipcMain.handle(\"ao:browser\", (_event, msg: BrowserMsg) => handleBrowser(msg));\n  registerMuxIpc();"
}

  "old_string": "    onAnnotation: (cb: (data: unknown) => void): (() => void) => {\n      const listener = (_e: unknown, d: unknown): void => cb(d);\n      ipcRenderer.on(\"ao:browser-annotation\", listener);\n      return () => ipcRenderer.removeListener(\"ao:browser-annotation\", listener);\n    },\n  },\n};",
  "new_string": "    onAnnotation: (cb: (data: unknown) => void): (() => void) => {\n      const listener = (_e: unknown, d: unknown): void => cb(d);\n      ipcRenderer.on(\"ao:browser-annotation\", listener);\n      return () => ipcRenderer.removeListener(\"ao:browser-annotation\", listener);\n    },\n  },\n\n  // The terminal mux (a WebSocket to the daemon's /mux, opened in main). Each\n  // method targets a session's pane by its runtime handle id.\n  mux: {\n    open: (handleId: string): Promise<void> =>\n      ipcRenderer.invoke(\"ao:mux:open\", handleId),\n    send: (handleId: string, data: string): Promise<void> =>\n      ipcRenderer.invoke(\"ao:mux:send\", handleId, data),\n    resize: (handleId: string, cols: number, rows: number): Promise<void> =>\n      ipcRenderer.invoke(\"ao:mux:resize\", handleId, cols, rows),\n    close: (handleId: string): Promise<void> =>\n      ipcRenderer.invoke(\"ao:mux:close\", handleId),\n    onData: (handleId: string, cb: (b64: string) => void): (() => void) => {\n      const channel = `ao:mux:msg:${handleId}`;\n      const listener = (_e: unknown, frame: { type?: string; data?: string }): void => {\n        if (frame.type === \"data\" && typeof frame.data === \"string\") cb(frame.data);\n      };\n      ipcRenderer.on(channel, listener);\n      return () => ipcRenderer.removeListener(channel, listener);\n    },\n    onExit: (handleId: string, cb: () => void): (() => void) => {\n      const channel = `ao:mux:msg:${handleId}`;\n      const listener = (_e: unknown, frame: { type?: string }): void => {\n        if (frame.type === \"exited\") cb();\n      };\n      ipcRenderer.on(channel, listener);\n      return () => ipcRenderer.removeListener(channel, listener);\n    },\n  },\n};"
}

Done. Here's where Task 4 v1 landed — built end-to-end on the `task4/in-app-browser` worktree, **uncommitted**.

## What's built

**Backend — fully tested, verified headlessly:**
- `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/annotations` — formats a captured element into an agent instruction and delivers it through the existing `Send` chain (→ zellij paste into the agent's pane). 3 controller tests prove the format + delivery; OpenAPI regenerated (parity + drift green); exposed `runtimeHandleId` on the session DTO so the in-app terminal can attach. Full backend build/vet/tests pass.

**Frontend — builds + typechecks clean (strict):**
- Electron `WebContentsView` in-app browser + a tiny preload + an **injected overlay** that captures `selector + classes + text` on click.
- A `ws`-based `/mux` relay so the renderer gets a live terminal.
- `BrowserPane` (URL bar, nav, **Annotate** toggle, bounds-sync) + a real **xterm Terminal** (from the emdash reference), tab-switched in `SessionView`. The overlay's capture is POSTed via `postAnnotation`.

## How it's verified — and the honest gaps

- **The data path is proven**: the controller test shows annotate → format → `Svc.Send`, and `Send → zellij paste` is the *existing, tested* `ao send` path. So an annotation reaching the agent's terminal is proven by composition.
- **I could not do the final GUI click-test** (no display for Electron here) or a **live agent receipt** — I spun up a real daemon and tried to spawn a session, but it failed with an env-specific internal error in the headless `/tmp` sandbox (zellij + git are present; my changes touch none of the spawn path and all backend tests pass). The full GUI demo is documented in `docs/design/in-app-browser.md` for your environment.
- **Least-verified piece:** the `Terminal.tsx` (xterm rendering + mux attach) builds and typechecks but I haven't run it live.

## To run the demo (in your env)
```bash
ao start && ao project add --path ~/Projects/yyork
( cd ~/Projects/yyork && pnpm web:dev )            # note the URL
( cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev )       # the desktop app
```
Spawn a session → open it → **Browser** tab → enter the URL → **Go** → **Annotate** → click an element → type an instruction. The **Terminal** tab (or `zellij attach <session>`) shows the agent receiving the `[ui-annotation] …` message.

## Two notes
- Your **`reverbcode` Zellij session is safe** — I verified it's still alive; my test cleanup ran in a separate socket dir.
- There's no `ao annotations` CLI yet — v1 has the browser POST directly to the daemon (the CLI/MCP *reader* is the documented fast-follow).

=== spawn order in the manager ===
func (m *Manager) Spawn(ctx context.Context, cfg ports.SpawnConfig) (domain.SessionRecord, error) {
	prompt, err := m.buildSpawnPrompt(ctx, cfg)
	if err != nil {
		return domain.SessionRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("spawn: prompt: %w", err)
	}

	rec, err := m.store.CreateSession(ctx, seedRecord(cfg, m.clock()))
	if err != nil {
		return domain.SessionRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("spawn: create: %w", err)
	}
	id := rec.ID

	branch := cfg.Branch
	if branch == "" {
		// A fresh, unique branch per session: gitworktree can't add a worktree on
		// a branch already checked out elsewhere (e.g. main), so default to one
		// derived from the assigned session id.
		branch = "ao/" + string(id)
	}
	ws, err := m.workspace.Create(ctx, ports.WorkspaceConfig{ProjectID: cfg.ProjectID, SessionID: id, Branch: branch})
	if err != nil {
		m.markSpawnFailedTerminated(ctx, id)
		return domain.SessionRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("spawn %s: workspace: %w", id, err)
	}

	agent, ok := m.agents.Agent(cfg.Harness)
	if !ok {
		_ = m.workspace.Destroy(ctx, ws)
		m.markSpawnFailedTerminated(ctx, id)
		return domain.SessionRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("spawn %s: no agent adapter for harness %q", id, cfg.Harness)
	}
	if err := m.prepareWorkspace(ctx, agent, id, ws.Path); err != nil {
		_ = m.workspace.Destroy(ctx, ws)
		m.markSpawnFailedTerminated(ctx, id)
		return domain.SessionRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("spawn %s: %w", id, err)
	}
	argv, err := agent.GetLaunchCommand(ctx, ports.LaunchConfig{
		SessionID:     string(id),
		WorkspacePath: ws.Path,
		Prompt:        prompt,
		IssueID:       string(cfg.IssueID),
	})
	if err != nil {
		_ = m.workspace.Destroy(ctx, ws)
		m.markSpawnFailedTerminated(ctx, id)
		return domain.SessionRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("spawn %s: launch command: %w", id, err)
	}
	handle, err := m.runtime.Create(ctx, ports.RuntimeConfig{
		SessionID:     id,
		WorkspacePath: ws.Path,
		Argv:          argv,
		Env:           spawnEnv(id, cfg.ProjectID, cfg.IssueID, m.dataDir),
	})
	if err != nil {
		_ = m.workspace.Destroy(ctx, ws)
		m.markSpawnFailedTerminated(ctx, id)
		return domain.SessionRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("spawn %s: runtime: %w", id, err)
	}

	metadata := domain.SessionMetadata{Branch: ws.Branch, WorkspacePath: ws.Path, RuntimeHandleID: handle.ID, Prompt: prompt}
	if err := m.lcm.MarkSpawned(ctx, id, metadata); err != nil {
		_ = m.runtime.Destroy(ctx, handle)
		_ = m.workspace.Destroy(ctx, ws)
		m.markSpawnFailedTerminated(ctx, id)
		return domain.SessionRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("spawn %s: completed: %w", id, err)
	}
	return m.getRecord(ctx, id)
}

func (c *SessionsController) spawn(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if c.Svc == nil {
		apispec.NotImplemented(w, r, "POST", "/api/v1/sessions")
		return
	}

		return
	}
	if len(in.Prompt) > maxPromptLen {

The decode and resize are actually correct — the mux **does** resize the PTY (`pty.Setsize`). So what you're seeing is the hard part: a **multi-layer rendering pipeline** — `xterm ← mux ← PTY ← zellij pane ← Claude's TUI` — and Claude Code is a heavy full-screen TUI. When xterm attaches, it replays the pane's buffered output (drawn at the *old* size) and Claude's full-width `─────` rules wrap and stack until a clean redraw. It's functional (live, interactive) but the rendering of a running TUI agent through that chain is genuinely messy.

## What that screenshot actually is
- The real, **live Claude Code agent** (`yyork-2`), interactive — you can type to it. It's flailing because my throwaway test spawn's prompt was literally `"demo"`, so it decided to go "launch the app" and probe port 3000. Garbage prompt, not a bug.
- The **garbled bits** (`25m|`, stacked `agent ─────` rules) are Claude's full-screen TUI rendered through a deep chain: `xterm ← mux ← PTY ← zellij pane ← Claude`. On attach, xterm replays the pane's *buffered* output (drawn at the old width) and Claude only repaints cleanly on a refresh/resize event — so the old-width rules wrap and pile up.

## Honest status
The terminal **functionally works** (live, full-screen, interactive, resize propagates). But clean rendering of a heavy TUI agent through this attach pipeline is a *real* task, not a one-line fix. `convertEol: false` is correct and helps line handling, but the stale-buffer/redraw mess needs a deliberate pass — most likely: on attach, after the resize, force Claude to repaint (clear xterm + a resize "wiggle" to trigger a full redraw), and possibly stop replaying stale scrollback.

# WebContentsView Summary

**What it is:** A View component that displays web content within an Electron application, inheriting from the `View` class.

**Deprecation note:** The documentation lists `BrowserView` as deprecated, suggesting `WebContentsView` is its modern replacement.

**Attachment & positioning:** Views are added to a window's content hierarchy using `win.contentView.addChildView(view)`, then positioned with the `setBounds()` method specifying coordinates and dimensions.

**Accessing webContents:** The `view.webContents` property provides access to the underlying WebContents object, enabling operations like `view.webContents.loadURL('https://example.com')`.

**Version info:** The documentation doesn't explicitly state the introduction version, though it's presented as current API in the latest docs.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the VS Code Simple Browser extension implementation regarding iframe and webview architecture:

## Simple Browser Extension Overview

The Simple Browser extension uses a webview to render webpages directly in VS Code. It provides a very basic browser preview using an iframe embedded in a webview.

## Architecture and Limitations

The browser has a number of limitations due to the security around iframes, including that it traps keyboard focus, can't detect if a page fails to load, and can't track the current url of the iframe.

## Webview Architecture Details

A webview is like an iframe within VS Code that your extension controls. A webview can render almost any HTML content in this frame, and it communicates with extensions using message passing.

## Implementation Pattern

Webviews are implemented as isolated environments that communicate with the workbench via an asynchronous messaging bridge. To ensure security and performance, webviews are hosted in iframe elements (even in Electron) and utilize Service Workers for local resource loading.

The Simple Browser extension represents a practical implementation of VS Code's webview API, using nested iframes to display external web content while maintaining the security isolation that VS Code requires for webview environments.

> AGENT

Done. Both typecheck and build pass. Here's what the redraw pass does and — honestly — how to confirm it, since I can't see your screen.

## What changed (`Terminal.tsx`)
On attach to a pane, after the initial size sync:
1. **Shrink by one column** → first SIGWINCH, the agent/zellij starts reacting.
2. **90ms later: `term.reset()` (wipe the stale snapshot) + restore the real size** → second SIGWINCH triggers a full repaint that streams back *right after* the clear — so no blank flash, and the old-width garbage (`25m|`, stacked `agent ─────`) gets overwritten by a clean full-width redraw.

Plus the earlier `convertEol: false` so raw PTY line-endings aren't re-munged.

## How to confirm (this part's yours — I can't see the GUI)
Your app is on Vite HMR, so it should pick this up. In the ReverbCode window:
1. **⌘R** to reload (ensures the new `Terminal.tsx` is live).
2. Open **yyork-2** again.
3. Watch the first ~½ second: it may flicker once as it repaints, then should settle into a **clean, full-width Claude TUI** — no stacked rules, no `25m|`.

**If it's still garbled after that:** that points to the deeper "rethink the terminal approach" path (streaming a zellij pane is the root mismatch — a direct PTY per agent would sidestep it). Tell me what you see and I'll go there instead of patching further.

One honest note: I verified the *logic and build*, not the pixels — the redraw-on-attach + resize-wiggle is the standard, well-understood fix for "attached to a running TUI looks like garbage," but your eyes on the reload are the real test.

=== ui/resizable.tsx ===
import type { ComponentProps } from "react";
import { GripVertical } from "lucide-react";
import { Panel, PanelGroup, PanelResizeHandle } from "react-resizable-panels";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

// shadcn/ui Resizable (https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/resizable),
// styled against our design tokens (--color-border / --color-ring). Wraps
// react-resizable-panels so the canvas split is draggable.

function ResizablePanelGroup({
  className,
  ...props
}: ComponentProps<typeof PanelGroup>) {
  return (
    <PanelGroup
      className={cn(
        "flex h-full w-full data-[panel-group-direction=vertical]:flex-col",
        className,
      )}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}

const ResizablePanel = Panel;

function ResizableHandle({
  withHandle,
  className,
  ...props
}: ComponentProps<typeof PanelResizeHandle> & { withHandle?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <PanelResizeHandle
      className={cn(
        "relative flex w-px items-center justify-center bg-border transition-colors after:absolute after:inset-y-0 after:left-1/2 after:w-1 after:-translate-x-1/2 hover:bg-ring focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-1 focus-visible:ring-ring data-[panel-group-direction=vertical]:h-px data-[panel-group-direction=vertical]:w-full data-[panel-group-direction=vertical]:after:left-0 data-[panel-group-direction=vertical]:after:h-1 data-[panel-group-direction=vertical]:after:w-full data-[panel-group-direction=vertical]:after:translate-x-0 data-[panel-group-direction=vertical]:after:-translate-y-1/2",
        className,
      )}
      {...props}
    >
      {withHandle && (
        <div className="z-10 flex h-5 w-3 items-center justify-center rounded-sm border border-border bg-elevated">
          <GripVertical className="h-2.5 w-2.5 text-muted" />
        </div>
      )}
    </PanelResizeHandle>
  );
}

export { ResizablePanelGroup, ResizablePanel, ResizableHandle };

import { clsx, type ClassValue } from "clsx";
import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge";

/** shadcn class-name helper: merge conditional + Tailwind classes safely. */
export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]): string {
  return twMerge(clsx(inputs));

// ── base64 ⇆ bytes (no Node Buffer in the sandboxed renderer) ───────────────

function base64ToBytes(b64: string): Uint8Array {
  const bin = atob(b64);
  const out = new Uint8Array(bin.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < bin.length; i++) out[i] = bin.charCodeAt(i);
  return out;
}


=== BrowserPane.tsx (full) ===
import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { postAnnotation, type BrowserAnnotation, type BrowserState } from "../lib/api";

// BrowserPane is the in-app browser surface. The actual page renders in a native
// WebContentsView owned by the Electron main process (see src/main.ts); this
// React component owns the chrome (URL bar, nav, annotate toggle) and keeps the
// view positioned over the `browser-slot` div via setBounds. The injected
// overlay captures element annotations, which arrive here and are POSTed to the
// session's agent. See docs/design/in-app-browser.md.
export function BrowserPane(props: {
  sessionId: string;
  onError: (msg: string) => void;
}) {
  const slotRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);
  const [urlInput, setUrlInput] = useState("http://localhost:5173");
  const [state, setState] = useState<BrowserState | null>(null);
  const [annotate, setAnnotate] = useState(false);
  const [toast, setToast] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const syncBounds = useCallback(() => {
    const el = slotRef.current;
    if (!el) return;
    const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    void window.ao.browser.control({
      type: "setBounds",
      bounds: {
        x: Math.round(r.left),
        y: Math.round(r.top),
        width: Math.round(r.width),
        height: Math.round(r.height),
      },
    });
  }, []);

  // Mount: position the view + subscribe to nav-state and annotation events.
  // Unmount (e.g. switching tabs): hide the native view.
  useEffect(() => {
    syncBounds();
    const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => syncBounds());
    if (slotRef.current) ro.observe(slotRef.current);
    window.addEventListener("resize", syncBounds);

    const offState = window.ao.browser.onState((s) => setState(s));
    const offAnnotation = window.ao.browser.onAnnotation((data: BrowserAnnotation) => {
      void postAnnotation(props.sessionId, data)
        .then(() =>
          setToast(`Sent “${data.note || data.element || data.selector}” to the agent`),
        )
        .catch((err) => props.onError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)));
    });

    return () => {
      ro.disconnect();
      window.removeEventListener("resize", syncBounds);
      offState();
      offAnnotation();
      void window.ao.browser.control({ type: "hide" });
    };
  }, [syncBounds, props]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!toast) return;
    const t = window.setTimeout(() => setToast(null), 3000);
    return () => window.clearTimeout(t);
  }, [toast]);

  const go = () => {
    const u = urlInput.trim();
    if (u) void window.ao.browser.control({ type: "navigate", url: u });
  };
  const toggleAnnotate = () => {
    const next = !annotate;
    setAnnotate(next);
    void window.ao.browser.control({ type: "setAnnotateMode", on: next });
  };

  return (
    <div className="browser-pane">
      <div className="browser-bar">
        <button
          className="icon-btn"
          onClick={() => void window.ao.browser.control({ type: "back" })}
          disabled={!state?.canGoBack}
          title="Back"
        >
          ‹
        </button>
        <button
          className="icon-btn"
          onClick={() => void window.ao.browser.control({ type: "forward" })}
          disabled={!state?.canGoForward}
          title="Forward"
        >
          ›
        </button>
        <button
          className="icon-btn"
          onClick={() => void window.ao.browser.control({ type: "reload" })}
          title="Reload"
        >
          ⟳
        </button>
        <input
          className="browser-url"
          value={urlInput}
          onChange={(e) => setUrlInput(e.target.value)}
          onKeyDown={(e) => e.key === "Enter" && go()}
          placeholder="http://localhost:5173"
          spellCheck={false}
        />
        <button className="btn-primary sm" onClick={go}>
          Go
        </button>
        <button
          className={annotate ? "btn-primary sm" : "btn-ghost sm"}
          onClick={toggleAnnotate}
          title="Toggle annotate mode, then click any element in the preview"
        >
          {annotate ? "● Annotating" : "Annotate"}
        </button>
      </div>
      <div className="browser-slot" ref={slotRef}>
        {!state?.url && (
          <div className="browser-hint">
            Enter a preview URL (your dev server) and press <b>Go</b>. Then toggle{" "}
            <b>Annotate</b> and click any element to send it to the agent.
          </div>
        )}
      </div>
      {toast && <div className="browser-toast">{toast}</div>}
    </div>
  );
}

Now I understand the layout and I see the likely **scroll** cause too: `.terminal-body` has `overflow: auto` *and* padding, which creates a second scroll container wrapping xterm's own `.xterm-viewport` — the wheel event gets eaten by the outer one instead of reaching xterm. I'll fix both. (Note: while Claude's full-screen TUI is active it's in the *alternate screen buffer*, which has no scrollback by design — xterm translates wheel→arrow keys so you scroll *within* Claude; that only works once the wrapper stops intercepting the wheel.)

> AGENT

All three are done. Here's the rundown:

## 1. Side-by-side resizable Terminal + Browser ✅
`TerminalView` now drops the Terminal/Browser tab toggle and renders both in a horizontal **shadcn `ResizablePanelGroup`** (which wraps `react-resizable-panels`, already a dep):
- **Left:** live agent Terminal (default 55%, min 25%)
- **`ResizableHandle withHandle`** — drag the grip to resize
- **Right:** in-app Browser (default 45%, min 25%)
- `autoSaveId="tr-split"` persists your split across reloads.

The native browser view tracks its panel via the existing ResizeObserver→setBounds, and the terminal refits on drag — both follow the handle live.

## 2. Terminal scroll fix ✅
The root cause: `.terminal-body` had `overflow: auto` **wrapping** xterm's own `.xterm-viewport` — a second scroll container that swallowed the wheel before it reached xterm (and its padding offset xterm's mouse coordinates). Removed the outer scroll; xterm now owns scrolling.
- One caveat that's *terminal physics, not a bug:* while Claude's full-screen TUI is active it's in the **alternate screen buffer**, which has no scrollback — xterm translates wheel→arrow-keys so you scroll *within* Claude. That now reaches it.

## 3. yyork started with the wrong command ✅
You were right. I had `cd ~/Projects/yyork/web && pnpm dev` = `vite dev` (**frontend only**, no backend, no `VITE_BACKEND_ORIGIN`). Fixed:
- Killed the stale frontend-only vite (was on :3000).
- Relaunched the correct **`pnpm dev` from the yyork root** (`scripts/yyork.mjs`) → full stack.
- **Verified:** web `:3000` serves `<title>yyork</title>`, backend `:7331` returns HTTP 200.
- Saved it to memory so I don't repeat it.

## To see it
**⌘R** in the ReverbCode window, open a session → you'll get the terminal + browser side by side. In the browser pane's URL bar, enter **`http://localhost:3000`** (the now-fully-working yyork) and hit Go, then toggle **Annotate**.

One small heads-up: the native browser view sits above the DOM, so the right ~half of the resize grip can underlap it — drag from the left side of the grip if it feels sticky. Want me to default the browser URL to `:3000` for the demo so there's no typing?

// AttachCommand returns the argv a human runs to attach their terminal to the
// session.
func (r *Runtime) AttachCommand(handle ports.RuntimeHandle) ([]string, error) {
	id, _, err := handleID(handle)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	args := append([]string{}, r.baseArgs()...)
	args = append(args, attachArgs(id)...)
	if r.socketDir == "" {
		return append([]string{r.binary}, args...), nil
	}
	return attachCommandWithEnv(r.binary, r.socketDir, args...), nil
}

func (r *Runtime) ensureSupportedVersion(ctx context.Context) error {
	out, err := r.run(ctx, versionArgs()...)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("zellij runtime: check version: %w", err)
	}
	if _, err := CheckVersionOutput(string(out)); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("zellij runtime: check version: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

func (r *Runtime) writeLayout(cfg ports.RuntimeConfig) (string, error) {
	file, err := os.CreateTemp(os.TempDir(), "ao-zellij-layout-*.kdl")
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("zellij runtime: create layout temp file: %w", err)
	}
	path := file.Name()
	if _, err := file.WriteString(buildLayout(cfg, r.shell)); err != nil {
		_ = file.Close()
		_ = os.Remove(path)
		return "", fmt.Errorf("zellij runtime: write layout temp file: %w", err)
	}
	if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
		_ = os.Remove(path)
		return "", fmt.Errorf("zellij runtime: close layout temp file: %w", err)
	}
	return path, nil

Now I have the real picture from the code. The mux **spawns a `zellij attach <session>` client** in a PTY and streams *that* to xterm (`AttachCommand` → `["attach", id]`). So the pipeline is:

`xterm ← WebSocket ← creack PTY ← zellij attach client ← background zellij session ← agent pane`

That's the root of the garbling: **zellij is re-rendering its own view on every size renegotiation**, and each redraw of the `agent` pane separator accumulates in xterm — and my resize-wiggle *added* renegotiations, likely making it worse, not better. xterm-side tweaks can't fix artifacts that originate from zellij's redraw stream. This is the "rethink the approach" path I flagged.

That's the answer: **emdash uses `node-pty`** — a *direct* PTY per agent (tmux optional, off by default). No double-rendering layer. That's why its terminal is clean. AO instead streams a `zellij attach` client, and zellij's own re-rendering is what stacks those `agent` separators in xterm. **xterm-side patches cannot fix this** — and my resize-wiggle actively made it worse by triggering extra zellij redraws.

> AGENT

Both pass. Stopgap is in: removed the wiggle (it was adding zellij redraws) and **debounced resize** so dragging the split no longer spams zellij. That'll calm the drag-induced stacking — but I want to be straight: **it won't fully clean it, because the root cause is architectural, not a tuning knob.**

Here's the definitive diagnosis, now grounded in both codebases:

| | How the agent terminal is rendered |
|---|---|
| **AO (reverbcode)** | daemon runs `zellij attach <session>` in a PTY → streams **zellij's rendering** to xterm. You're rendering a renderer. zellij repaints its whole view on every resize, and those repaints pile up → the stacked `agent ─────` separators. |
| **emdash (your ref)** | `node-pty` owns a **direct PTY** per agent (tmux optional, off by default). Single render → clean. |

The kicker: AO's terminal manager **already uses `creack/pty`** (a direct PTY, with `pty.Setsize`) — it's just pointing that PTY at a `zellij attach` client instead of at the agent. So the clean path is within reach; it's a question of *what the PTY runs*.

=== the func bodies ===
func attachCommandWithEnv(binary, socketDir string, args ...string) []string {
	if socketDir == "" {
		return append([]string{binary}, args...)
	}
	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
		command := strings.Builder{}
		command.WriteString("$env:ZELLIJ_SOCKET_DIR = ")
		command.WriteString(psQuote(socketDir))
		command.WriteString("; & ")
		command.WriteString(psQuote(binary))
		for _, arg := range args {
			command.WriteByte(' ')
			command.WriteString(psQuote(arg))
		}
		return []string{"powershell.exe", "-NoLogo", "-NoProfile", "-Command", command.String()}
	}
	return append([]string{"env", "ZELLIJ_SOCKET_DIR=" + socketDir, binary}, args...)
}
func (r *Runtime) baseArgs() []string {
	args := []string{}
	if r.configDir != "" {
		args = append(args, "--config-dir", r.configDir)
	}
	return args
}

> AGENT

**Definitive answer.** The clean `dump-screen` shows the agent pane content is *fine* — normal Claude output with one of *its own* `─────` rules. The word **"agent" is NOT in the content.** And `pane_content_x: 1` confirms a **1-cell frame is being drawn** around the pane. So:

> The stacked **`agent ─────`** is the **zellij pane frame + title**, rendered by the attach client and streamed to xterm — *not* the agent's output. `--pane-frames false` is set at session *creation*, but the **attaching client re-enables frames** because `AttachCommand` doesn't pass that option.

That's the real fix: pass `--pane-frames false` on the *attach*. Let me confirm the mux uses `AttachCommand`:

> AGENT

Stopped and cleaned up. Here's the resolution — and this time it's **proven, not guessed.**

## Root cause (definitively diagnosed)
The garbled green **`agent ─────`** lines are the **zellij pane frame + title bar**, drawn by the streamed `zellij attach` client — **not the agent's output.** Evidence:
- **`dump-screen` of yyork-2's pane**: the actual content is clean Claude output; the word **"agent" doesn't appear in it.**
- **`list-panes`**: `pane_content_x: 1` — a 1-cell border on every side = **a frame is being drawn**, even though `--pane-frames false` is set at session *creation*.
- The reason: the **attaching client re-enables frames** because `AttachCommand` only ran `zellij attach <id>` with no options. Every repaint re-draws that bordered `agent` title → it stacks in xterm.

## The fix
**Backend (`zellij` adapter):**
1. `attachArgs` → `attach <id> options --pane-frames false` — the streamed client draws **no frame**. (The actual fix.)
2. Layout → `default_tab_template { children }` — also strips the tab-bar/status-bar chrome.

**Frontend (`Terminal.tsx`):** reverted the counterproductive resize-wiggle, **debounced** resize (dragging the split no longer spams zellij with redraws), one-shot scrollback clear on attach, `convertEol: false`, and removed the outer `overflow` wrapper (your scroll fix).

## Validation
- Backend builds; **zellij package tests pass**; the new layout KDL **parsed successfully** in an isolated socket.
- The one failing test, `TestSessionStreamsRealZellijPane`, **fails identically with my change stashed** — it's a pre-existing macOS long-`$TMPDIR` zellij-socket issue, not my edit.

## Two things to know
- **The backend fix needs the daemon rebuilt + a *fresh* attach** to show — your existing `yyork-2` was attached the old way. And heads-up: the demo sessions now read **`(EXITED)`** (resurrectable). That wasn't my commands — everything I ran on that socket was read-only (`list`/`dump`); the agent exited on its own at the `pnpm install` prompt.
- Frontend tweaks apply on **⌘R**.

Want me to **rebuild the demo daemon with these fixes and spawn one fresh session** so you can see the terminal render clean (no `agent` frame) end-to-end? That's the real proof — say go and I'll do it carefully (isolated demo daemon, never touching your `reverbcode` session).

Root cause nailed: the `WebContentsView` is owned by the **main process**, not React. On a ⌘R / Vite full reload, the renderer is destroyed **without** running `BrowserPane`'s unmount cleanup, so the native view is orphaned — still visible, floating over the fresh Board. The `hide` only ever happens from the renderer, which is gone.

Fix: tear the view down in the main process whenever the renderer reloads:

> TOOL

So the "Failed to load sessions: 500" in that overlay was a **transient** (the browser had loaded the yyork page during the window when I killed the stale vite and the real stack was still booting). A refresh clears it.

The real bug — the overlay floating over your Board — is fixed.

## What happened
The in-app browser is a native `WebContentsView` **owned by the main process**, composited *above* the DOM. When the renderer reloads (⌘R, or a Vite full-reload after one of my HMR edits) while the browser was visible, React is destroyed **without** running `BrowserPane`'s cleanup — so the native view is orphaned: still visible, floating over whatever loads next, with nothing left to hide it. That's the yyork page bleeding over your Board.

## Fix (two layers)
1. **Renderer (`App.tsx`)** — on every fresh mount, send `browser.control({ type: "destroy" })`. The *current* main process already handles `destroy`, so this clears any orphaned view **immediately on ⌘R — no Electron restart needed.**
2. **Main (`main.ts`)** — tear the view down on `did-start-loading` of the main frame, so a reload can never orphan it again. (Belt-and-suspenders; takes effect after the next Electron restart, since main-process code doesn't hot-reload.)

Both typecheck and build clean.

## To clear it now
**⌘R** in the ReverbCode window. The new `App.tsx` will tell the main process to destroy the stuck view on mount, and your Board will be clean. (⌘R *was* the thing orphaning it; now it's the thing that fixes it.)

So where we are: the terminal frame fix (backend) is ready but needs a daemon rebuild + fresh session to see; this overlay fix lands on ⌘R. package terminal

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/coder/websocket"
)

const (
	defaultCols        = 100
	defaultRows        = 30
	defaultIdleTimeout = 30 * time.Second
	defaultScrollback  = 10000
	clientBufferChunks = 64
)

// AttachStrategy selects how the Manager bridges a WebSocket connection to the
// underlying Zellij session.
type AttachStrategy string

const (
	// StrategyPerClient is Option A: every WebSocket connection spawns its OWN
	// `zellij attach` process (its own PTY). Zellij itself maintains the screen
	// state and redraws the full screen on every attach, so a fresh per-client
	// attach is a faithful repaint for free — no shared process, no scrollback
	// buffer, no server-side emulator. The Manager only tracks logical sessions
	// for idle bookkeeping.
	StrategyPerClient AttachStrategy = "per-client"

	// StrategyEmulator is Option B: one SHARED `zellij attach` process per
	// session feeds all PTY output into a server-side `vt` emulator that keeps
	// the authoritative live screen. On attach, a client receives a faithful
	// repaint SNAPSHOT (alt-screen mode + grid + cursor + scrollback) rather
	// than a raw byte tail, then streams live deltas.

That's the answer in black and white. yyork offers two strategies; the elegant one is **StrategyPerClient**: each WebSocket connection spawns its **own** `zellij attach` process, so zellij does a **full clean repaint at that client's exact size for free** — no shared session, no scrollback tail, no size negotiation, no garbling. reverbcode currently *shares* one attach across clients and streams the raw byte tail — exactly the cause of my garbling.
