15	// Option A — per-client attach.
16	//
17	// Each WebSocket connection gets its OWN `zellij attach` process (its own
18	// PTY). Zellij is a multiplexer whose core job is maintaining the session's
19	// screen state and redrawing the FULL screen whenever a client attaches, so a
20	// fresh per-connection attach IS a faithful repaint for free — no byte replay,
21	// no scrollback buffer, no fan-out.
22	//
23	// The Manager only tracks logical sessions for idle bookkeeping. Closing an
24	// attach process detaches that single client; it never kills the session.
25	
26	// serveWSPerClient registers the connection for idle bookkeeping, spawns its
27	// own attach process, and pipes PTY <-> WebSocket.
28	func (m *Manager) serveWSPerClient(conn *websocket.Conn, cfg SessionConfig) {
29		cfg = withDefaults(cfg)
30		if cfg.ID == "" {
31			_ = conn.Close(websocket.StatusInternalError, "terminal session id is required")
32			return
33		}
34		if err := m.ctx.Err(); err != nil {
35			_ = conn.Close(websocket.StatusInternalError, err.Error())
36			return
37		}
38	
39		// Register this connection against its logical session so idle cleanup can
40		// track when the last client leaves. This does NOT start a process.
41		key := terminalKey(cfg)
42		sess := m.acquire(key)
43		defer m.release(key, sess)
44	
45		// Each connection spawns its OWN attach process. A fresh attach is a
46		// faithful Zellij redraw of the current screen — no replay needed.
47		process, err := m.runner.Start(m.ctx, StartOptions{
48			Command: cfg.Command,
49			CWD:     cfg.CWD,
50			Cols:    cfg.InitialCols,
51			Env:     cfg.Env,
52			Rows:    cfg.InitialRows,
53		})
54		if err != nil {
55			slog.Warn("failed to start terminal attach", "session_id", cfg.ID, "error", err)
56			_ = conn.Close(websocket.StatusInternalError, "failed to start terminal")
57			return
58		}
59	
60		client := newClientAttach(process)
61		if err := client.pipe(conn); err != nil && !isExpectedWebsocketClose(err) {
62			slog.Debug("terminal websocket closed", "session_id", cfg.ID, "error", err)
63		}
64	}
65	
66	// acquire returns the logical session for key, creating it if needed, and
67	// increments its live-client count.
68	func (m *Manager) acquire(key string) *session {
69		m.mu.Lock()
70		defer m.mu.Unlock()
71	
72		sess := m.perClient[key]
73		if sess == nil {
74			sess = &session{}
75			m.perClient[key] = sess
76		}
77		sess.cancelIdle()
78		sess.clients++
79		return sess
80	}
81	
82	// release decrements the live-client count for key. When the last client
83	// leaves, the logical session is scheduled for removal after the idle delay.
84	// Removing the session entry does NOT touch the Zellij session — the zellij
85	// server keeps it alive independently.
86	func (m *Manager) release(key string, sess *session) {
87		m.mu.Lock()
88		defer m.mu.Unlock()
89	
90		if sess.clients > 0 {
91			sess.clients--
92		}
93		if sess.clients > 0 {
94			return
95		}
96	
97		if m.idleDelay <= 0 {
98			if m.perClient[key] == sess {
99				delete(m.perClient, key)
100			}
101			return
102		}
103	
104		sess.idleTimer = time.AfterFunc(m.idleDelay, func() {
105			m.mu.Lock()
106			defer m.mu.Unlock()
107			if m.perClient[key] == sess && sess.clients == 0 {
108				delete(m.perClient, key)
109			}
110		})
111	}
112	
113	// session is pure bookkeeping for a logical terminal. It owns no process and
114	// no scrollback; it just counts live attach connections so the Manager knows
115	// when a session has gone idle. The actual screen state lives in the Zellij
116	// server, reached anew by each per-client attach process.
117	type session struct {
118		clients   int
119		idleTimer *time.Timer
120	}
121	
122	// cancelIdle stops any pending idle-removal timer. Callers must hold the
123	// Manager mutex.
124	func (s *session) cancelIdle() {
125		if s.idleTimer != nil {
126			s.idleTimer.Stop()
127			s.idleTimer = nil
128		}
129	}
130	
131	// clientAttach is a thin PTY <-> WebSocket pipe bound to a single connection's
132	// own attach process.
133	type clientAttach struct {
134		process Process
135	}
136	
137	func newClientAttach(process Process) *clientAttach {
138		return &clientAttach{process: process}
139	}
140	
141	// pipe streams the attach process's PTY output to conn, forwards conn input
142	// and resize control messages to the process, and tears the process down when
143	// the connection ends. Closing the attach process detaches this client only;
144	// the Zellij session survives.
145	func (c *clientAttach) pipe(conn *websocket.Conn) error {
146		conn.SetReadLimit(64 * 1024)
147	
148		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
149		defer cancel()
150	
151		// Closing the process unblocks the writer's PTY read and detaches this
152		// client from Zellij. It does NOT kill the Zellij session.
153		defer func() { _ = c.process.Close() }()
154	
155		writerDone := make(chan error, 1)
156		go func() {
157			writerDone <- c.writeToConn(ctx, conn)
158		}()
159	
160		readErr := c.readFromConn(ctx, conn)
161		cancel()
162		_ = conn.Close(websocket.StatusNormalClosure, "")
163	
164		select {
165		case writerErr := <-writerDone:
166			return errors.Join(readErr, writerErr)
167		case <-ctx.Done():
168			return errors.Join(readErr, ctx.Err())
169		}
170	}
171	
172	// writeToConn copies PTY output straight to the WebSocket. There is no replay
173	// buffer: the first bytes a client receives are Zellij's fresh repaint.
174	func (c *clientAttach) writeToConn(ctx context.Context, conn *websocket.Conn) error {
175		buf := make([]byte, 32*1024)
176		for {
177			n, err := c.process.Read(buf)
178			if n > 0 {
179				if writeErr := conn.Write(ctx, websocket.MessageBinary, buf[:n]); writeErr != nil {
180					return writeErr
181				}
182			}
183			if err != nil {
184				if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
185					return conn.Close(websocket.StatusNormalClosure, "terminal detached")
186				}
187				if ctx.Err() != nil {
188					return nil
189				}
190				return conn.Close(websocket.StatusInternalError, err.Error())
191			}
192			if ctx.Err() != nil {
193				return ctx.Err()
194			}
195		}
196	}
197	
198	func (c *clientAttach) readFromConn(ctx context.Context, conn *websocket.Conn) error {
199		for {
200			messageType, payload, err := conn.Read(ctx)
201			if err != nil {
202				return err
203			}
204	
205			switch messageType {
206			case websocket.MessageBinary:
207				if _, err := c.process.Write(payload); err != nil {
208					return err
209				}
210			case websocket.MessageText:
211				if err := c.handleControl(payload); err != nil {
212					return err
213				}
214			}
215		}
216	}
217	
218	func (c *clientAttach) handleControl(payload []byte) error {
219		var message controlMessage
220		if err := json.Unmarshal(payload, &message); err != nil {
221			return fmt.Errorf("decode terminal control message: %w", err)
222		}
223	
224		switch message.Type {
225		case "resize":
226			if message.Cols <= 0 || message.Rows <= 0 {
227				return errors.New("terminal resize requires positive cols and rows")
228			}
229			return c.process.Resize(message.Cols, message.Rows)
230		default:
231			return fmt.Errorf("unknown terminal control message %q", message.Type)
232		}
233	}
234

Before I go further on the terminal port — let me address your blinking question, because it's a clear, separate bug I can see immediately.

**Why the in-app browser blinks:** `BrowserPane`'s main `useEffect` has `props` in its dependency array. `props` is a brand-new object on every render, and `TerminalView` re-renders every 2s (the `getSession` poll). So the effect **tears down and re-runs on every render** — and its cleanup calls `browser.control({ type: "hide" })`, then setup calls `syncBounds` → `setBounds` + `setVisible(true)`. Hide→show, hide→show = the blink.

106		if len(command) == 0 {
107			return defaultShell()
108		}
109		if command[0] == "" {
110			return "", nil, errors.New("terminal command path is required")
111		}

114	}

116	func defaultShell() (string, []string, error) {
117		if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
118			for _, candidate := range []struct {
119				name string
120				args []string
121			}{
122				{name: "pwsh.exe", args: []string{"-NoLogo"}},
123				{name: "powershell.exe", args: []string{"-NoLogo"}},
124				{name: "cmd.exe"},
125			} {
126				path, err := exec.LookPath(candidate.name)
127				if err == nil {
128					return path, candidate.args, nil
129				}
130			}
131	
132			return "", nil, errors.New("no supported Windows shell found")
133		}
134	
135		if shell := os.Getenv("SHELL"); shell != "" {
136			if filepath.IsAbs(shell) {
137				if _, err := os.Stat(shell); err == nil {
138					return shell, nil, nil
139				}
140			}
141			if path, err := exec.LookPath(shell); err == nil {
142				return path, nil, nil
143			}
144		}
145	
146		if path, err := exec.LookPath("sh"); err == nil {
147			return path, nil, nil
148		}
149	
150		return "", nil, errors.New("no supported shell found")
151	}
152	
153	func mergeTerminalEnv(base []string, extra []string) []string {
154		env := append([]string(nil), base...)
155		if runtime.GOOS != "windows" {
156			env = upsertEnv(env, "TERM=xterm-256color")
157		}
158	
159		for _, value := range extra {
160			env = upsertEnv(env, value)
161		}
162	
163		return env
164	}
165	
166	func upsertEnv(env []string, value string) []string {
167		keyEnd := -1
168		for index, char := range value {
169			if char == '=' {
170				keyEnd = index
171				break
172			}
173		}
174		if keyEnd <= 0 {
175			return env
176		}
177	
178		keyPrefix := value[:keyEnd+1]
179		for index, current := range env {
180			if len(current) >= len(keyPrefix) && current[:len(keyPrefix)] == keyPrefix {
181				env[index] = value
182				return env
183			}
184		}
185	
186		return append(env, value)
187	}

110	// openSession returns the live session for id, starting it on first open. The id
111	// is the runtime handle id (Zellij handle).
112	func (m *Manager) openSession(id string) (*session, error) {
113		m.mu.Lock()
114		defer m.mu.Unlock()
115		if m.closed {
116			return nil, context.Canceled
117		}
118		if s, ok := m.sessions[id]; ok {
119			return s, nil
120		}
121		handle := ports.RuntimeHandle{ID: id}
122		s := newSession(id, handle, m.src, m.spawn, m.log)
123		m.sessions[id] = s
124		go func() {
125			s.run(m.ctx)
126			m.mu.Lock()
127			if cur, ok := m.sessions[id]; ok && cur == s {
128				delete(m.sessions, id)
129			}
130			m.mu.Unlock()
131		}()
132		return s, nil
133	}

135	// Serve runs the protocol loop for one client connection until it errors, the
136	// client disconnects, or ctx/the manager is cancelled. It owns the single writer
137	// goroutine and the heartbeat.
138	func (m *Manager) Serve(ctx context.Context, conn wsConn) {
139		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
140		defer cancel()
141	
142		c := &connState{
143			mgr:    m,
144			conn:   conn,
145			cancel: cancel,
146			out:    make(chan serverMsg, defaultWriteBuffer),
147			terms:  map[string]func(){},
148		}
149		defer c.cleanup()
150	
151		go c.writeLoop(ctx)
152		go c.heartbeatLoop(ctx, m.heartbeat)
153	
154		for {
155			var msg clientMsg
156			if err := conn.ReadJSON(ctx, &msg); err != nil {
157				return
158			}
159			if ctx.Err() != nil {
160				return
161			}
162			c.handle(msg)
163		}
164	}
165	
166	// connState is the per-connection mutable state.
167	type connState struct {
168		mgr    *Manager
169		conn   wsConn
170		cancel context.CancelFunc
171		out    chan serverMsg
172	
173		mu        sync.Mutex
174		terms     map[string]func() // terminal id -> unsubscribe
175		unsubEvts func()
176		closed    bool
177	}
178	
179	func (c *connState) handle(msg clientMsg) {
180		switch msg.Ch {
181		case chTerminal:
182			c.handleTerminal(msg)
183		case chSubscribe:
184			c.handleSubscribe(msg)
185		case chSystem:
186			if msg.Type == msgPing {
187				c.enqueue(serverMsg{Ch: chSystem, Type: msgPong})
188			}
189		}
190	}
191	
192	func (c *connState) handleTerminal(msg clientMsg) {
193		switch msg.Type {
194		case msgOpen:
195			c.openTerminal(msg.ID)
196		case msgData:
197			raw, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(msg.Data)
198			if err != nil {
199				return
200			}
201			if s := c.lookup(msg.ID); s != nil {
202				_ = s.write(raw)
203			}
204		case msgResize:
205			if s := c.lookup(msg.ID); s != nil {
206				_ = s.resize(msg.Rows, msg.Cols)
207			}
208		case msgClose:
209			c.closeTerminal(msg.ID)
210		}
211	}

213	func (c *connState) openTerminal(id string) {
214		if id == "" {
215			c.enqueue(serverMsg{Ch: chTerminal, Type: msgError, Error: "missing terminal id"})
216			return
217		}
218		c.mu.Lock()
219		if _, ok := c.terms[id]; ok {
220			c.mu.Unlock()
221			return // already open on this conn; avoid duplicate replay
222		}
223		c.mu.Unlock()
224	
225		s, err := c.mgr.openSession(id)
226		if err != nil {
227			c.enqueue(serverMsg{Ch: chTerminal, ID: id, Type: msgError, Error: err.Error()})
228			return
229		}

232		// data/exited frames subscribe delivers (the single out channel preserves
233		// this order). Reversing it would let a reconnecting client with buffered

14	// PTYSource is what a terminal needs from the runtime: the argv that attaches a
15	// PTY to a session's pane, and a liveness check used to decide whether a dropped
16	// PTY should be re-attached or treated as a clean exit. The Zellij runtime adapter
17	// satisfies this via AttachCommand/IsAlive; the interface lives here, next to its
18	// only consumer, so terminal does not depend on a concrete adapter.
19	type PTYSource interface {
20		AttachCommand(handle ports.RuntimeHandle) ([]string, error)
21		IsAlive(ctx context.Context, handle ports.RuntimeHandle) (bool, error)
22	}
23	
24	// ptyProcess is a started PTY-backed attach process. It is the injection seam
25	// that keeps fan-out, buffering, and re-attach testable without a real process:
26	// unit tests supply a scripted in-memory implementation; production uses a
27	// creack/pty-backed one (see pty_unix.go).
28	type ptyProcess interface {
29		io.ReadWriteCloser
30		Resize(rows, cols uint16) error
31	}
32	
33	// spawnFunc starts a PTY for argv. ctx cancellation must terminate the process.
34	type spawnFunc func(ctx context.Context, argv []string) (ptyProcess, error)
35	
36	// reattach policy: a PTY that drops is re-attached while the underlying Zellij
37	// session is still alive, up to maxReattach consecutive failures. An attach that
38	// survived longer than reattachResetGrace before dropping resets the counter, so
39	// a long-lived pane that blips recovers but a tight crash-loop gives up.
40	const (
41		defaultMaxReattach       = 5
42		defaultReattachResetTime = 5 * time.Second
43	)
44	
45	// subscriber receives one terminal's output frames. It must not block: session
46	// fan-out calls subscribers while serializing replay/delivery under its mutex,
47	// so the WS layer funnels frames onto its own buffered writer.
48	type subscriber func(data []byte)
49	
50	// session is one attached terminal pane, fanned out to N subscribers. It owns a
51	// single PTY (re-attached on drop) and a replay ring buffer.
52	type session struct {
53		id     string
54		handle ports.RuntimeHandle
55		src    PTYSource
56		spawn  spawnFunc
57		log    *slog.Logger
58		ring   *ringBuffer
59	
60		maxReattach int
61		resetGrace  time.Duration
62	
63		mu       sync.Mutex
64		pty      ptyProcess
65		subs     map[int]subscriber
66		exitSubs map[int]func()
67		nextSub  int
68		closed   bool
69		exited   bool
70	
71		doneOnce sync.Once
72		done     chan struct{}
73	}
74	
75	func newSession(id string, handle ports.RuntimeHandle, src PTYSource, spawn spawnFunc, log *slog.Logger) *session {
76		if log == nil {
77			log = slog.Default()
78		}
79		return &session{
80			id:          id,
81			handle:      handle,
82			src:         src,
83			spawn:       spawn,
84			log:         log,
85			ring:        newRingBuffer(defaultRingMax),
86			maxReattach: defaultMaxReattach,
87			resetGrace:  defaultReattachResetTime,
88			subs:        map[int]subscriber{},
89			exitSubs:    map[int]func(){},
90			done:        make(chan struct{}),
91		}
92	}
93	
94	// run drives attach → read-loop → re-attach until the pane exits cleanly, the
95	// session is closed, or ctx is cancelled. It is started once per session.
96	func (s *session) run(ctx context.Context) {
97		defer s.markDone()
98	
99		failures := 0
100		for {
101			if s.isClosed() || ctx.Err() != nil {
102				return
103			}
104	
105			argv, err := s.src.AttachCommand(s.handle)
106			if err != nil {
107				s.fail("attach command: " + err.Error())
108				return
109			}
110			p, err := s.spawn(ctx, argv)
111			if err != nil {
112				failures++
113				if !s.shouldReattach(ctx, failures) {
114					s.fail("spawn pty: " + err.Error())
115					return
116				}
117				continue
118			}
119	
120			s.setPTY(p)
121			start := time.Now()
122			s.copyOut(p)
123			_ = p.Close()
124	
125			if time.Since(start) >= s.resetGrace {
126				failures = 0
127			}
128			failures++
129	
130			if !s.shouldReattach(ctx, failures) {
131				s.markExited()
132				return
133			}
134			s.log.Debug("terminal re-attaching", "id", s.id, "failures", failures)
135		}
136	}
137	
138	// copyOut pumps PTY output into the ring buffer and out to subscribers until the
139	// PTY closes or errors.
140	func (s *session) copyOut(p ptyProcess) {
141		buf := make([]byte, 32*1024)
142		for {
143			n, err := p.Read(buf)
144			if n > 0 {
145				chunk := make([]byte, n)
146				copy(chunk, buf[:n])
147				s.deliver(chunk)
148			}
149			if err != nil {
150				return
151			}
152		}
153	}
154	
155	// shouldReattach decides whether a dropped/failed PTY warrants another attempt:
156	// only while not closed/cancelled, the Zellij session still exists, and we are
157	// under the consecutive-failure cap. A backoff sleep separates attempts.
158	func (s *session) shouldReattach(ctx context.Context, failures int) bool {
159		if s.isClosed() || ctx.Err() != nil || failures > s.maxReattach {
160			return false
161		}
162		alive, err := s.src.IsAlive(ctx, s.handle)
163		if err != nil || !alive {
164			return false
165		}
166		select {
167		case <-ctx.Done():
168			return false
169		case <-time.After(reattachBackoff(failures)):
170			return true
171		}
172	}
173	
174	func reattachBackoff(failures int) time.Duration {
175		d := time.Duration(failures) * 200 * time.Millisecond
176		if d > time.Second {
177			d = time.Second
178		}
179		return d
180	}
181	
182	// subscribe registers an output callback and an exit callback, replays the ring
183	// buffer to the new subscriber, and returns an unsubscribe func. If the pane has
184	// already exited, onExit fires immediately and exited is true; the caller must
185	// not treat the returned no-op unsubscribe as a live registration (there is
186	// nothing to track and re-opening must stay possible).
187	func (s *session) subscribe(onData subscriber, onExit func()) (unsubscribe func(), exited bool) {
188		s.mu.Lock()
189		if s.exited {
190			s.mu.Unlock()
191			if onExit != nil {
192				onExit()
193			}
194			return func() {}, true
195		}
196		id := s.nextSub
197		s.nextSub++
198		s.subs[id] = onData
199		if onExit != nil {
200			s.exitSubs[id] = onExit
201		}
202		// Deliver the replay while still holding s.mu. deliver (the copyOut path)
203		// also takes s.mu around append+fanout, so the two are fully serialized: a
204		// chunk is either in this snapshot (and was fanned out before this
205		// subscriber registered) or it is fanned out after this returns, never both.
206		// Releasing the lock before replaying would let a chunk land in both the
207		// snapshot and a concurrent fanout, delivering it twice (or let an exit
208		// frame overtake the replay). onData is a non-blocking enqueue, so holding
209		// the lock across it cannot deadlock.
210		replay := s.ring.snapshot()
211		if len(replay) > 0 {
212			onData(replay)
213		}
214		s.mu.Unlock()
215	
216		return func() {
217			s.mu.Lock()
218			delete(s.subs, id)
219			delete(s.exitSubs, id)
220			s.mu.Unlock()
221		}, false
222	}
223	
224	// deliver appends a chunk to the ring and fans it out to current subscribers as
225	// one atomic step under s.mu. Holding the lock across both is what lets
226	// subscribe (which snapshots + replays under the same lock) guarantee
227	// exactly-once delivery: append+fanout and register+snapshot+replay can never
228	// interleave. Each fn is a non-blocking enqueue, so the lock is held only
229	// briefly and cannot deadlock.
230	func (s *session) deliver(chunk []byte) {
231		s.mu.Lock()
232		defer s.mu.Unlock()
233		s.ring.append(chunk)
234		for _, fn := range s.subs {
235			fn(chunk)
236		}
237	}
238	
239	// write sends client keystrokes to the PTY. It is a no-op if no PTY is attached.
240	func (s *session) write(p []byte) error {
241		s.mu.Lock()
242		pty := s.pty
243		s.mu.Unlock()
244		if pty == nil {
245			return errors.New("terminal: no active pty")
246		}
247		_, err := pty.Write(p)
248		return err
249	}
250	
251	func (s *session) resize(rows, cols uint16) error {
252		s.mu.Lock()
253		pty := s.pty
254		s.mu.Unlock()
255		if pty == nil {
256			return nil
257		}
258		return pty.Resize(rows, cols)
259	}
260	
261	func (s *session) setPTY(p ptyProcess) {
262		s.mu.Lock()
263		s.pty = p
264		s.mu.Unlock()
265	}
266	
267	// close tears the session down: stop re-attaching and kill the PTY.
268	func (s *session) close() {
269		s.mu.Lock()
270		if s.closed {
271			s.mu.Unlock()
272			return
273		}
274		s.closed = true
275		pty := s.pty
276		s.pty = nil
277		s.mu.Unlock()
278		if pty != nil {
279			_ = pty.Close()
280		}
281	}
282	
283	func (s *session) isClosed() bool {
284		s.mu.Lock()
285		defer s.mu.Unlock()
286		return s.closed
287	}
288	
289	func (s *session) isExited() bool {
290		s.mu.Lock()
291		defer s.mu.Unlock()
292		return s.exited
293	}
294	
295	// markExited flips the pane to exited and notifies/clears subscribers.
296	func (s *session) markExited() {
297		s.mu.Lock()
298		if s.exited {
299			s.mu.Unlock()
300			return
301		}
302		s.exited = true
303		exits := make([]func(), 0, len(s.exitSubs))
304		for _, fn := range s.exitSubs {
305			exits = append(exits, fn)
306		}
307		s.exitSubs = map[int]func(){}
308		s.mu.Unlock()
309		for _, fn := range exits {
310			fn()
311		}
312	}
313	
314	// fail reports an unrecoverable attach error to subscribers as an exit.
315	func (s *session) fail(reason string) {
316		s.log.Warn("terminal session failed", "id", s.id, "reason", reason)
317		s.markExited()
318	}
319	
320	func (s *session) markDone() { s.doneOnce.Do(func() { close(s.done) }) }
321

Now I see the full picture. The garbling has **two** sources, and yyork eliminates both:
1. **The frame** — fixed (`--pane-frames false` on attach).
2. **The ring-buffer replay on `subscribe`** (`s.ring.snapshot()` → `onData(replay)`) — on every reconnect it replays accumulated raw bytes (old frame redraws at old sizes). yyork explicitly has **"no byte replay"**: each WS spawns its own fresh `zellij attach`, and zellij's repaint *is* the initial state.

So the port is: make reverbcode **per-client** — each terminal open spawns its own attach (no shared `m.sessions`, no ring replay). Let me read the rest of the manager to wire it correctly:

275		// no-op (the key did not exist yet), so the assign above just resurrected a
276		// stale entry for a dead pane. Re-apply the delete while still holding c.mu.
277		if exitFired {

2	
3	import (
4		"context"

12	)

14	// EventSource is the session-state feed the "sessions" channel forwards. The CDC
15	// broadcaster satisfies it; the interface lives next to its consumer so terminal
16	// does not depend on CDC internals beyond the Event shape.
17	type EventSource interface {
18		Subscribe(fn func(cdc.Event)) (unsubscribe func())
19	}
20	
21	// wsConn is the transport seam: a JSON-framed, single-reader/single-writer
22	// WebSocket connection. internal/httpd adapts coder/websocket to this; tests
23	// supply an in-memory fake. WriteJSON is only ever called from the per-conn
24	// writer goroutine; Ping may be called concurrently (it is a control frame).
25	type wsConn interface {
26		ReadJSON(ctx context.Context, v any) error
27		WriteJSON(ctx context.Context, v any) error
28		Ping(ctx context.Context) error
29		Close(reason string) error
30	}
31	
32	const (
33		defaultHeartbeat   = 15 * time.Second
34		defaultWriteBuffer = 1024
35	)
36	
37	// Manager owns the set of live terminal sessions and serves WebSocket clients.
38	// Sessions outlive any single connection: multiple clients can attach to the
39	// same pane, and a client reconnect re-subscribes to the existing session.
40	type Manager struct {
41		src       PTYSource
42		events    EventSource
43		spawn     spawnFunc
44		log       *slog.Logger
45		heartbeat time.Duration
46	
47		// ctx scopes every session's PTY lifetime; cancelled by Close.
48		ctx    context.Context
49		cancel context.CancelFunc
50	
51		mu       sync.Mutex
52		sessions map[string]*session
53		closed   bool
54	}
55	
56	// Option configures a Manager.
57	type Option func(*Manager)
58	
59	// WithSpawn overrides the PTY spawner (tests inject a fake).
60	func WithSpawn(fn spawnFunc) Option { return func(m *Manager) { m.spawn = fn } }
61	
62	// WithHeartbeat overrides the ping interval.
63	func WithHeartbeat(d time.Duration) Option { return func(m *Manager) { m.heartbeat = d } }
64	
65	// NewManager builds a Manager. src attaches PTYs; events feeds the session
66	// channel (may be nil to disable it). A nil logger falls back to slog.Default.
67	func NewManager(src PTYSource, events EventSource, log *slog.Logger, opts ...Option) *Manager {
68		if log == nil {
69			log = slog.Default()
70		}
71		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
72		m := &Manager{
73			src:       src,
74			events:    events,
75			spawn:     defaultSpawn,
76			log:       log,
77			heartbeat: defaultHeartbeat,
78			ctx:       ctx,
79			cancel:    cancel,
80			sessions:  map[string]*session{},
81		}
82		for _, opt := range opts {
83			opt(m)
84		}
85		return m
86	}
87	
88	// Close tears down every session and stops re-attach loops. Safe to call once on
89	// daemon shutdown.
90	func (m *Manager) Close() {
91		m.mu.Lock()
92		if m.closed {
93			m.mu.Unlock()
94			return
95		}
96		m.closed = true
97		sessions := make([]*session, 0, len(m.sessions))
98		for _, s := range m.sessions {
99			sessions = append(sessions, s)
100		}

func (m *Manager) ServeWS(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, cfg SessionConfig) {
	conn, err := websocket.Accept(w, r, &websocket.AcceptOptions{
		OriginPatterns: []string{
			"localhost:*",
			"127.0.0.1:*",
			"[::1]:*",
			"http://localhost:*",
			"http://127.0.0.1:*",
			"http://[::1]:*",
		},
	})
	if err != nil {
		slog.Warn("failed to accept terminal websocket", "session_id", cfg.ID, "error", err)
		return
	}
	defer conn.Close(websocket.StatusNormalClosure, "")

	switch m.strategy {
	case StrategyPerClient:
		m.serveWSPerClient(conn, cfg)
	default:
		m.serveWSEmulator(conn, cfg)
	}
}
